beisong.baogong.end: The forged deeds are exposed and the river cleared; nobles and eunuchs back off, and the capital says no bribes reach old King Yama Bao.
shots: The main gate of Kaifeng prefecture opened wide
Petitioners walk straight to the hall to state their case
Along the Huimin River, nobles' gardens encroach on the channel
The figures on the deed show signs of tampering
The gardens are demolished and the river cleared
beisong.baogong.title: Lord Bao Governs Kaifeng: Bao Zheng

beisong.beijiu.end: The generals resign their commands and receive rich rewards; the guards are split into three commands and Song civil rule over the military begins.
shots: The Bianjing palace after evening court
Zhao Pu warns: the guard commanders must be considered
A palace banquet with veteran generals seated in rows
Deep in the wine, Taizu sends the attendants away
Next day the generals plead illness
beisong.beijiu.title: Releasing Military Power over Wine: Emperor Taizu of Song

beisong.bisheng.end: Bi Sheng tried wooden type too, but uneven grain swelled with water and stuck to the paste; after his death his clay type passed to Shen Kuo's kinsmen, who kept it as a treasure.
shots: In a printing shop carved wooden blocks are stacked to the ceiling, each good for a single page
A commoner craftsman shapes small squares of clay and carves a reversed character into each, thin as a coin's rim
The furnace fires the clay type hard and the pieces are filed one by one into wooden racks
On an iron plate spread with resin, wax and paper ash the type fills a frame, is warmed over fire and pressed flat as a whetstone
Two iron plates take turns, one printing while the other is set, and sheet after sheet is peeled away
beisong.bisheng.title: Clay Movable Type: Bi Sheng

beisong.chanyuan.end: Song and Liao swear the Chanyuan treaty with annual silver and silk; there is no major war for over a century.
shots: The two towns of Chanzhou on either bank of the Yellow River
The Liao army sweeps south
At court some urge moving the capital south
The emperor crosses the river and mounts the north wall; troops see the yellow dragon banner
One shot from the great crossbow
beisong.chanyuan.title: The Treaty of Chanyuan

beisong.diqing.end: By the third watch the pass is taken; Song cavalry crush Nong Zhigao at Guiren and Lingnan is pacified.
shots: Kunlun Pass hidden in hills outside Binzhou
Di Qing executes thirty-two officers who disobeyed orders
Binzhou hangs lanterns for three nights of the Lantern Festival
At the second watch Di Qing leaves the feast pleading illness
Crossing Kunlun Pass on a night of wind and rain
beisong.diqing.title: Seizing Kunlun Pass by Night: Di Qing

beisong.fangla.end: Han Shizhong takes Fang La alive but another commander steals the credit; Fang La is executed, and whether Song Jiang joined the campaign is disputed.
shots: Deep in the lacquer groves of Qingxi in Muzhou
Flower-and-rock convoys sail north on the canal
On the Haizhou coast Zhang Shuye burns the rebels' boats
Han Shizhong creeps along the stream and asks a village woman the way
Fang La is captured alive in Bangyuan Cave
beisong.fangla.title: Bangyuan Cave: Fang La and Song Jiang

beisong.fanzhongyan.end: Fan serves on in Hangzhou and Qingzhou and dies at Xuzhou in 1052; the reforms fail, but Wang Anshi takes them up again two decades later, and "first to worry, last to rejoice" becomes the scholar's creed.
shots: On the walls of Yanzhou the northwest wind whips sand as a civil official inspects the forts
In the Tianzhang Pavilion the emperor hands him brush and paper and presses him to write down his reforms
At court the officials he has cut stand grim-faced as rumours call them a faction
In his Dengzhou study he unrolls a painting of Dongting Lake sent by an old friend in Yuezhou
He writes the final line: be first to worry for the world, and last to enjoy its pleasures
beisong.fanzhongyan.title: First to Worry: Fan Zhongyan and the Qingli Reforms

beisong.haoshuichuan.end: Ren Fu fights to the death with a dozen arrows in him; after more defeats Song and Xia make peace in 1044.
shots: Haoshui River below the Liupan mountains
Han Qi warns Ren Fu: disobey orders and you die even in victory
Sealed silver-clay boxes lie by the road
The boxes open and over a hundred pigeons fly up
The Xia army closes in on every side
beisong.haoshuichuan.title: Haoshui River: Li Yuanhao

beisong.huizong.end: In the 1126 siege the Genyue's trees are cut for firewood and its rocks broken into catapult stones; Zhu Mian is exiled and executed, and a year later both emperors are carried north by the Jin.
shots: By Lake Tai hundreds of labourers haul a huge rock from the lakebed with ropes
Rock barges choke the Bian Canal; bridges are torn down and city gates cut open to let them pass
Northeast of Kaifeng an artificial mountain rises day by day, stocked with rare birds and beasts
In a pavilion the emperor takes up his brush and writes the mountain's name in lean, hard strokes
Beacon fires flare in the north; he hands the throne to the crown prince and leaves the capital by night
beisong.huizong.title: The Flower and Rock Convoys: Emperor Huizong and the Genyue

beisong.jingkang.end: In 1127 Jin carries off both emperors and the court; Northern Song ends and Prince Kang takes the throne at Yingtian.
shots: Bustling streets of Bianjing
Jin troops march south; Huizong abdicates
Li Gang defends the city and Jin withdraws for now
Winter, a second siege; Guo Jing opens the gate to fight
The city falls; two emperors are taken north
beisong.jingkang.title: The Jingkang Disaster: Two Emperors Taken North

beisong.liuhou.end: Preserved in mercury and dressed as an empress dowager, she lies unchanged; the emperor sighs that rumours cannot be trusted, treats the Liu clan more generously still, and honours his mother as empress dowager.
shots: In a side hall of the inner palace a maid holding a newborn hands the child to the empress's people
Behind the screen the empress dowager sits in ceremonial robes while the young emperor stands before it
A silent woman walks among the palace women at the late emperor's tomb and never speaks
The chief minister kneels before the screen: the consort must be buried with first-rank rites, her coffin filled with mercury
The emperor opens the coffin himself and finds his mother's face as if alive
beisong.liuhou.title: A Civet Cat for the Crown Prince: Empress Dowager Liu and Consort Li

beisong.ouyangxiu.end: The 1057 roll includes Su Shi, Su Zhe, Zeng Gong, Zhang Zai and Cheng Hao; failed candidates jeer at Ouyang in the street, but from then on examination prose turns plain.
shots: Thousands of candidates file into the examination hall while the examiners wait behind the screen
The chief examiner lifts his red brush and strikes through a paper full of strange characters from top to bottom
Another paper has the examiners slapping the table, and Mei Yaochen carries it to the chief examiner
Suspecting it is by his own protégé Zeng Gong, the examiner ranks it only second to avoid favouritism
The sealed name is opened and reads: Su Shi
beisong.ouyangxiu.title: The Roll of a Thousand Years: Ouyang Xiu Sets the Exam

beisong.shenkuo.end: The Liao claim fails and Shen presents his map of the journey; later at Yanzhou he studies the local "rock oil", and after the fall of Yongle in 1082 he is demoted and writes the Dream Pool Essays in retirement.
shots: In the Bureau of Military Affairs archive an official searches roll by roll through the dust
He finds an old boundary agreement naming the ancient Great Wall as the line, while the Liao claim land south of it
With the document and his escort he rides north through snow, recording every mountain and river
In the Liao tent the chief minister questions him again and again, and he answers each point from the documents
At last the Liao have nothing left to say; he rolls up the document, rises and takes his leave
beisong.shenkuo.title: The Old Files of the Bureau: Shen Kuo's Embassy to Liao

beisong.simaguang.end: Shenzong dies the next year; Sima Guang becomes chief minister and abolishes nearly all the new laws, Wang Anshi sighs "even this too?" and dies, and Sima dies in office a few months later.
shots: At court two old friends quarrel bitterly over the new laws, and one leaves the capital
In the Garden of Solitary Delight in Luoyang a study lamp burns all night between bamboo and herb beds
The compilers turn thirteen centuries of events into long drafts, the manuscripts piling up across the rooms
He revises a draft again and again in neat script without a single cursive stroke
Nineteen years on, 294 scrolls are delivered to the palace
beisong.simaguang.title: My Strength Is Spent: Sima Guang and the Comprehensive Mirror

beisong.wutai.end: Pardoned with help from the dowager and ministers, Su Shi is banished to Huangzhou, where he farms the eastern slope and calls himself Dongpo.
shots: An envoy bursts into the Huzhou office with two guards
An official boat goes north up the canal under pale moonlight by Lake Tai
Censorate cells, crows crowding the cypress trees
A fish lies in the lunch box his son delivers
In prison he writes farewell poems to his brother
beisong.wutai.title: The Crow Terrace Poetry Case: Su Shi

beisong.xining.end: Wang Anshi resigns twice; after Shenzong's death Sima Guang scraps the reforms and factional strife lasts until the dynasty's end.
shots: Bianjing in 1069
Emperor and minister discuss what comes first
Green Sprouts, hired service, baojia—one new law after another
Drought and the Picture of Refugees
Reformers against conservatives
beisong.xining.title: The Xining Reforms: Wang Anshi

beisong.yangye.end: No help comes; Yang Ye is captured and starves himself to death, and the officers who abandoned him are punished.
shots: Beyond Yanmen Pass, the four prefectures of Huan, Shuo, Yun and Ying
Cao Bin is beaten at Qigou; the western army is ordered to escort civilians south
Wang Shen taunts: you are called the Invincible
Yang Ye points to Chenjiagu: set crossbows here to support me
At Langya village he suffers dozens of wounds
beisong.yangye.title: Chenjiagu: Yang Ye

beisong.zhuying.end: Zhao Guangyi takes the throne as Emperor Taizong and changes the era that same year; three years later Taizu's son Dezhao takes his own life after a rebuke, and two years after that Defang dies of illness.
shots: Snow has fallen all night on Kaifeng and the palace eaves are piled with white
In the Wansui Hall two brothers drink together, their shadows cast on the paper window
The candle shadows waver and a jade-handled axe strikes into the snow
Near dawn a eunuch leaves the palace through the snow but does not go to the prince's mansion
Seeing that the man entering is the Prince of Jin, the empress falters and then speaks
beisong.zhuying.title: Candle Shadows and the Sound of an Axe: The Death of Taizu

chunqiu.baolixi.end: Duke Mu gives Baili Xi the government of Qin and calls him the Minister of Five Ram Skins; on his advice Jian Shu is brought in as a senior minister, and Qin begins its rise over the Western Rong.
shots: On the outskirts of Wan in Chu, a white-haired old man drives an ox along a field ridge
A Qin envoy holds up five black ram skins and tells the Chu men he has come to ransom a runaway slave
In the palace at Yong, Duke Mu of Qin unties the old man's ropes himself
Ruler and minister sit facing each other for three days and nights as the bamboo slips pile up
The old man rises and bows: "I am not the equal of my friend Jian Shu."
chunqiu.baolixi.title: Five Ram Skins: Baili Xi

chunqiu.changshao.end: The Qi army breaks and is pursued; three years later Cao Mo seizes Duke Huan with a dagger at Ke and land is returned.
shots: The field of Changshao, two armies facing each other
Cao Gui asks: on what will you fight?
Qi drums once; Lu does not move
Qi drums a third time; Cao Gui says: now
He sees their tracks confused and banners drooping
chunqiu.changshao.title: One Drum Roll of Courage: the Battle of Changshao

chunqiu.chencai.end: Confucius laughs at Yan Hui's answer; Zigong reaches Chu, King Zhao sends troops to escort them, and the party escapes.
shots: On open ground between Chen and Cai, a train of carts is surrounded in the wilds
On the seventh day the disciples lie in the grass too weak to rise
Zilu comes in angry: does a gentleman also come to the end of his road?
Beside the cart the master plays the qin, and the music does not stop
Yan Hui comes in and says: the master's Way is too great for the world to hold
chunqiu.chencai.title: Starving Between Chen and Cai: Confucius on the Road

chunqiu.chengpu.end: The Chu army is defeated and Ziyu kills himself; Duke Wen gathers the lords at Jiantu and is named hegemon.
shots: Nineteen years of exile along endless hills
At the Chu feast the king asks how he will repay him
Chong'er returns home across the river
At Chengpu the Jin army falls back ninety li
Horses draped in tiger skins; the Chu right wing collapses
chunqiu.chengpu.title: Retreating Three Stages: the Battle of Chengpu

chunqiu.hongshui.end: Song is routed and the duke wounded; he dies of the wound the next summer. "No drums before the enemy is in ranks" becomes a line argued over for two thousand years.
shots: On the north bank of the Hong the Song army has formed up, banners taut in the winter wind
Across the river the Chu army begins to wade over, men and horses crowding mid-stream
Marshal Ziyu rides up to the chariot: they are many, we are few, strike before they finish crossing
Chu lands but has not yet formed ranks; Ziyu begs again, and the duke still shakes his head
Chu's line is formed, drums thunder, the Song ranks break and an arrow strikes the duke in the thigh
chunqiu.hongshui.title: The Battle of the Hong River: Duke Xiang's Benevolence

chunqiu.huangong.end: At Kuiqiu the lords honour Qi; Duke Huan becomes the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn era.
shots: A long road across the plain outside Linzi
Two princes race home; Guan Zhong shoots an arrow
Bao Shuya recommends Guan Zhong and Duke Huan forgives his enemy
North against the Mountain Rong, south to rebuke Chu
The covenant at Kuiqiu
chunqiu.huangong.title: Honour the King, Repel the Barbarians: Duke Huan of Qi

chunqiu.jiagu.end: The Qi ruler backs down; an armed ambush is defused by Confucius through ritual alone.
shots: In the hills of Jiagu two altars face each other
Confucius stands beside the Duke of Lu and straightens his robes
To the drums, Lai men rush the altar with weapons
Confucius shields the duke and rebukes them sternly
Qi returns the lands of Yun, Huan and Guiyin
chunqiu.jiagu.title: The Meeting at Jiagu: Confucius Leads the Rites

chunqiu.jiezitui.end: The duke cannot find him and grants the land of Mianshang in his name, "to record my fault." The Zuo zhuan and the Shiji end there; neither mentions burning the hill.
shots: Outside the palace gate at Jiang, the companions of exile queue for rewards amid carts and horses
A gaunt middle-aged man stands apart from the crowd, turns and walks away
In a thatched hut his old mother asks: shouldn't you at least tell him?
Mother and son shoulder a little grain and walk into the deep hills of Mianshang
The duke's carriage reaches the foot of the mountain and finds only cloud and mist
chunqiu.jiezitui.title: Fire on Mianshang: Jie Zitui

chunqiu.laozi.end: Laozi finishes two books, some five thousand words on the Way and Virtue, then leaves, and no one knows where he ends. Sima Qian records two other candidates and admits no one can say which is true.
shots: In the royal archive at Luoyi, bamboo slips are stacked to the roof beams
A middle-aged visitor from Lu respectfully asks about the rites; the old man says only a few words
Years later the old man rides a black ox slowly toward the western pass
The pass keeper stops him: Master, you are going into hiding, write a book for me first
The first line is brushed onto the slips: "The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way."
chunqiu.laozi.title: Purple Air from the East: Laozi Leaves Through the Pass

chunqiu.wending.end: Wangsun Man answers that Heaven's mandate remains and the cauldrons' weight may not be asked; Chu withdraws.
shots: Bells and drums in the palace at Ying day and night
Wu Ju speaks in riddles: a bird that neither flies nor sings for three years
Attacking the Rong of Luhun, the army reaches the Luo River
Parading troops on Zhou soil; Wangsun Man comes to greet them
The size and weight of the cauldrons
chunqiu.wending.title: Asking About the Cauldrons: King Zhuang of Chu

chunqiu.wuyue.end: In 473 BCE Yue destroys Wu and Fuchai kills himself; Fan Li leaves office and Wen Zhong is forced to die.
shots: Mist over Lake Tai, hills like eyebrows
After the battle of Fujiao the king of Yue retreats to Kuaiji
Suing for peace at Kuaiji: Wen Zhong's humble words
Gall hung by his seat, he tastes it sitting or lying
The Yue army crosses the river
chunqiu.wuyue.title: Sleeping on Brushwood, Tasting Gall: Wu and Yue

chunqiu.xiaozhi.end: Jin defeats Qin at Xiao and captures three generals; freed at Wen Ying's request, they are met by Duke Mu in mourning white.
shots: At the Qin gate an old man holds back his son who is marching out
Qin chariots pass the royal city; soldiers leap aboard showing off
On the road to Hua a Zheng merchant drives twelve oxen to meet them
In the gorges of Mount Xiao Jin troops wait in ambush on both sides
Jin attacks; not a horse or chariot of Qin escapes
chunqiu.xiaozhi.title: Xian Gao Feeds the Army: the Battle of Xiao

chunqiu.yanzi.end: Duke Jing understands and lightens his punishments; the Zuo zhuan says the words of a humane man bring wide benefit.
shots: In the markets of Linzi, Yanzi's old house is squeezed against the noisy bazaar
Duke Jing sends word: your house is damp and loud, move somewhere high and dry
Yanzi declines; the duke laughs: living by the market, do you know what is dear and what is cheap?
Shoe stalls are piled high with shoes, while crowds buy artificial feet for those whose feet were cut off as punishment
Yanzi answers: "Artificial feet are dear, shoes are cheap."
chunqiu.yanzi.title: Feet Dear, Shoes Cheap: Yanzi

chunqiu.zhaoguan.end: Wu troops enter Ying; Wu Zixu digs up King Ping's corpse and flogs it, as the Shiji records.
shots: Chu hills and a pass between two mountains
King Ping believes slander and summons Wu She's two sons
Wu Shang goes to his death; Wu Yuan draws his bow and refuses
Pursuers behind at Zhao Pass; a fisherman on the river
One battle at Boju and the capital Ying falls
chunqiu.zhaoguan.title: Zhao Pass: Wu Zixu

chunqiu.zhaoshi.end: Duke Jing restores Zhao Wu and his lands; Zhao Wu later leads Jin and hosts the disarmament conference.
shots: Armoured troops surround the Zhao mansion in Xintian three deep
A woman carrying a child hides in the duke's palace
Zhao lands are handed to others
Han Jue reminds the duke of Zhao Cui and Zhao Dun
The child is brought before the ministers; the Zhao are restored
chunqiu.zhaoshi.title: The Xiagong Massacre: the Orphan of Zhao

chunqiu.zhengbo.end: In the tunnel mother and son recite verses of joy and are reconciled as before.
shots: The Zheng capital Xinzheng, distant hills beyond the walls
Lady Jiang asks for Jing for Duan; Zhai Zhong warns the walls are too long
Duan at Jing repairs armour and gathers chariots
Zifeng leads two hundred chariots and the people of Jing desert Duan
Not until the Yellow Springs shall we meet again
chunqiu.zhengbo.title: Meeting His Mother Underground: Duke Zhuang of Zheng

chunqiu.zhuanzhu.end: The dagger pierces King Liao's armour and the guards cut Zhuan Zhu down; Prince Guang's hidden soldiers pour out and he takes the throne as King Helü.
shots: In the Wu capital, King Liao's guards line both sides of the road from the palace to Prince Guang's gate
At the banquet every servant is searched, guards with long blades flank the aisle
Prince Guang complains of a sore foot, leaves the table and slips down into the cellar
A cook carries a roast fish up to the hall, its belly slightly swollen
He tears open the fish and draws a dagger
chunqiu.zhuanzhu.title: A Blade in the Fish: Zhuan Zhu Kills King Liao

chunqiu.zichan.end: Zichan replies that he cannot provide for future generations, he is only trying to save his own age. Twenty years later Jin casts its own law cauldron.
shots: In the village school of the Zheng capital, gentlemen gather to debate the government's merits
Minister Ranming advises: better to tear the school down
Zichan waves the idea away: these people are my teachers
Six years later, founders pour the text of the laws into a great bronze cauldron
A letter arrives from Jin; Shuxiang writes that once people know the laws they will no longer fear their betters
chunqiu.zichan.title: Casting the Penal Code: Zichan of Zheng

donghan.baimasi.end: The temple is named White Horse Temple; there the two monks translate the Sutra in Forty-Two Sections, usually seen as the arrival of Buddhism in the Central Plains, though a Yuezhi envoy had already recited Buddhist texts to a Han scholar decades earlier.
shots: Deep in the Southern Palace the emperor dreams of a golden man with a halo, flying before the hall
At court a minister says: in the west there is a god called the Buddha
The envoys' camels and horses cross the snowy Pamirs, heading ever west
On the road back a white horse carries the scriptures, two foreign monks walking alongside
Outside the west gate of Luoyang the bell of the first Buddhist temple rings
donghan.baimasi.title: The White Horse Carries the Sutras: Seeking the Dharma

donghan.banchao.end: Shanshan submits and sends a hostage; Ban Chao spends thirty years in the Western Regions and becomes Protector General.
shots: A copyist's desk in a Luoyang office
He throws down his brush and sighs
Shanshan: the king's courtesy suddenly cools
Thirty-six men, night, a strong wind
Fire set downwind
donghan.banchao.title: Throwing Down the Brush: Ban Chao in the Western Regions

donghan.banzhao.end: Ban Zhao completes the eight tables, Ma Xu finishes the treatise on astronomy, and when she dies in her seventies the empress dowager mourns her in plain white.
shots: In a Luoyang prison an unfinished manuscript lies scattered on the floor
In the Dongguan library a middle-aged woman takes up her brush among stacks of bamboo slips
The young empress and consorts sit around her listening to her lectures
Below the gallery kneels a young scholar copying every line she reads aloud
The last cell of the eight tables is filled and she lays down her brush
donghan.banzhao.title: Finishing the Book of Han: Ban Zhao

donghan.danggu.end: Li Ying, Fan Pang and over a hundred die in prison; the ban lasts until the Yellow Turbans rise.
shots: The Imperial Academy in Luoyang with thirty thousand students
Li Ying executes Zhang Cheng's son; eunuchs accuse the partisans
Northern prison: shackles and hoods
Chen Fan leads eighty officers sword in hand through the Chengming Gate
Fan Pang bids farewell to his mother
donghan.danggu.title: The Proscription of Partisans: Li Ying and Fan Pang

donghan.dongxuan.end: The emperor laughs that a Son of Heaven is not a commoner, frees the stiff-necked magistrate and rewards him; Dong Xuan shares it with his clerks.
shots: Luoyang, the Xia Gate pavilion
Dong Xuan stops the carriage and draws a line on the ground with his knife
The princess returns to complain to the emperor
Dong Xuan beats his head against a pillar, blood streaming
Hands on the ground, he will not bow
donghan.dongxuan.title: The Stiff-Necked Magistrate: Dong Xuan

donghan.huangjin.end: Zhang Jue dies of illness and his brothers are killed; the main Yellow Turban force falls, but the realm descends into chaos.
shots: A year of disaster, withered yellow fields
The Way of Great Peace: talisman water cures, followers flock in
Gates marked in white clay: jiazi
Thirty-six divisions rise on one day in yellow headscarves
Changshe: fire sweeps the grass camp
donghan.huangjin.title: The Blue Heaven Is Dead: the Yellow Turban Rising

donghan.kunyang.end: Wang Xun is killed and the Xin army breaks; so many drown that the Zhi stops flowing, and Wang Mang dies the same year.
shots: The small town of Kunyang by the Zhi River
The Xin army, said to be a million, stretches a thousand li
Liu Xiu and twelve riders leave by the south gate at night
Three thousand volunteers charge the enemy centre
Thunder and wind; roof tiles fly
donghan.kunyang.title: The Battle of Kunyang: Thunderstorm Breaks the Xin Army

donghan.liangji.end: Liang Ji and his wife kill themselves, their fortune of three billion cash halves the empire's taxes, and the five eunuchs who brought him down usher in the age of eunuch power.
shots: At court in the Southern Palace an eight-year-old sits on the throne, staring at the generalissimo below
The child says: this is a domineering general
That afternoon a bowl of boiled cakes is set before the little emperor
Thirteen years later, deep in the night, an emperor bites a eunuch's arm to seal a blood oath
A thousand guards surround the Liang mansion and its great gate slams shut
donghan.liangji.title: The Domineering General: Liang Ji

donghan.mayuan.end: Ma Yuan dies of disease on campaign; slandered over a cartload of seeds, he is stripped of honours until his name is later cleared.
shots: Tower ships and warships advance in a Jiaozhi bay
In a fever-ridden forest soldiers fall one by one
At a victory feast an old general raises his cup
Sixty-two-year-old Ma Yuan vaults onto his horse and looks around
Below Mount Hutou the current is too strong for the boats
donghan.mayuan.title: Wrapped in Horsehide: General Fubo

donghan.wangmang.end: A merchant kills Wang Mang on Jian Terrace; the Xin falls after fifteen years.
shots: Weiyang Palace in Chang'an, the Han ancestral temples
The Empress Dowager hurls the imperial seal to the ground
Land nationalised, slave sales banned; coinage changed again and again
Lülin and Red Eyebrows rise everywhere
Jian Terrace surrounded by water, besieged hundreds deep
donghan.wangmang.title: The Xin Dynasty: Wang Mang's Reforms

donghan.yanguang.end: Yan Guang refuses office and farms at Mount Fuchun; his fishing spot becomes Yanling Rapids, and he dies at eighty.
shots: In a great Qi marsh a man in a sheepskin coat sits fishing
A carriage with silk gifts; envoys go back and forth three times
In the palace the emperor and a commoner share a bed
The astrologer rushes in: a guest star has crossed the imperial seat
A single fishing boat on the Fuchun River
donghan.yanguang.title: A Guest Star Crosses the Throne: Yan Ziling

donghan.yangzhen.end: Wang Mi leaves ashamed; Yang Zhen later rises to Grand Commandant, is dismissed after impeaching the eunuchs and takes poison west of Luoyang.
shots: At a posthouse in Changyi, late at night, a county magistrate knocks softly at the door with a bundle
The bundle opens and ten jin of gold gleams in the lamplight
The magistrate whispers: it is night, no one will know
The old governor points at the sky, then at the ground
He pushes the bundle back: Heaven knows, the spirits know, I know, you know
donghan.yangzhen.title: Heaven Knows, Earth Knows: Yang Zhen's Four Knowings

donghan.yanran.end: The stone is carved and the army returns; Dou Xian later falls for treason and Ban Gu dies in prison.
shots: Northern steppe and the Khangai mountains
Three columns meet at Mount Zhuoye
At Mount Jiluo the northern chanyu flees
They climb Mount Yanran, three thousand li beyond the frontier
Ban Gu composes the inscription carved into the rock
donghan.yanran.title: Carving the Stone at Yanran: Dou Xian's Campaign

donghan.zaozhi.end: Days later a courier confirms the Longxi earthquake; all admire it and the court begins recording quake directions.
shots: Smoke rises over the imperial workshops in Luoyang
Bark, hemp, rags and fishing nets pounded into pulp
The pulp is sheeted and dried: the first sheet of paper
The seismoscope: eight dragons holding balls, toads below
One dragon drops its ball: an earthquake in the west
donghan.zaozhi.title: Paper and the Seismoscope: Cai Lun and Zhang Heng

liangjin.bawang.end: One prince after another seizes power until 306; the north is ruined and Liu Yuan's Xiongnu have already risen.
shots: The Luoyang palace, bronze camels in the lanes
Empress Jia issues a secret edict at night
Prince Lun of Zhao ascends the throne as officials kneel, Sun Xiu at his side
Princes' armies fight year after year around Luoyang
At Dangyin arrows rain down; an official spreads his arms to shield the emperor
liangjin.bawang.title: The War of the Eight Princes

liangjin.daoyun.end: Sun En, moved, spares the child; widowed, Xie Daoyun lives on at Kuaiji, and the governor who visits leaves in admiration of her conversation.
shots: In the Xie courtyard, heavy snow falling, children gather round their uncle to discuss literature
The uncle asks what the falling snow is like; a boy says: salt tossed into the air
A girl answers: better to say willow catkins rising on the wind
Forty years later Kuaiji falls; amid the flames she draws a knife and charges out with her maids
Facing the rebel leader she stands holding her grandson: this concerns the Wang house, not other clans
liangjin.daoyun.title: Willow Catkins on the Wind: Xie Daoyun

liangjin.doufu.end: Twenty years later Sun Xiu demands Lüzhu; she leaps from the tower and Shi Chong is executed at the Eastern Market.
shots: Forty li of purple silk screens outside Luoyang
Fifty li of brocade screens set against them
Wang Kai presents a coral tree two feet tall
Shi Chong smashes it with an iron ruyi
On a tower in the Golden Valley Garden a woman steps to the railing
liangjin.doufu.title: The Shattered Coral: Shi Chong and Wang Kai Compete in Wealth

liangjin.feishui.end: The Qin army flees, taking every sound for pursuit; Xie An reads the victory report over a game of go: the boys have beaten them.
shots: Outside Shouyang: Mount Bagong and the Fei River
The Former Qin host marches south, banners within sight of each other
Fu Jian sees every tree on the mountain as a soldier
Qin pulls back slightly and cannot stop retreating
Wind and cranes' cries
liangjin.feishui.title: Every Rustle an Enemy: the Battle of the Fei River

liangjin.huanwen.end: Huan Wen burns his boats and retreats, loses thirty thousand men, and his prestige never recovers.
shots: Elders of Guanzhong greet the army by the roadside with oxen and wine
In the Bashang camp a man in coarse cloth picks lice while discussing the realm
Fifteen years later the willows at Jincheng are ten spans round
At Fangtou the Jin grain boats are cut off
On the Xiangyi road Yan cavalry spring an ambush
liangjin.huanwen.title: Even Trees Grow Old: Huan Wen's Northern Campaigns

liangjin.lanting.end: The preface becomes the famous Lanting Preface; two years later Wang Xizhi resigns and vows never to serve again.
shots: Lofty peaks, dense woods and tall bamboo at Shanyin
Clear rushing streams reflect on either side
A wine cup floats downstream—before whom will it stop?
Wang Xizhi writes on inspiration
Life and death are great matters indeed
liangjin.lanting.title: The Orchid Pavilion: the Ninth Year of Yonghe

liangjin.liuyu.end: Yao Hong surrenders and Later Qin falls; Liu Yu returns south and founds the Song in 420.
shots: The Yellow River and the Wei; Chang'an in sight
Army and fleet advance together upriver
The crescent formation: two thousand men, a hundred wagons
Boats glide on the Wei with no rowers visible
The gates of Chang'an swing open
liangjin.liuyu.title: Swallowing Ten Thousand Li: Liu Yu's Northern Campaign

liangjin.taoqian.end: Tao returns to farming and never serves again; picking chrysanthemums by the eastern fence, he gazes at the southern hills.
shots: Autumn at the Pengze county office
A clerk says he must dress formally to greet the inspector
He hands back his seal and leaves that day
The boat drifts lightly, the wind lifts his robe
The paths are overgrown, yet pine and chrysanthemum remain
liangjin.taoqian.title: Home Again: Tao Yuanming

liangjin.xinting.end: Wang Dao declines — if the sun shared its light with all things, what would the people look up to? — and people say "the Wang and the Sima share the realm".
shots: South of Jiankang, at the Xinting pavilion above the river, émigré gentlemen sit drinking on the ground
One famous scholar gazes at the river and sighs: the scenery is no different, only the rivers and mountains have changed
They look at one another and weep; some cover their faces and sob
The chancellor strikes the table and rises, his face hardening
A year later at the enthronement, the emperor tugs the chancellor's sleeve, asking him to share the imperial couch
liangjin.xinting.title: Weeping at Xinting: Wang and Sima Share the Realm

liangjin.yongjia.end: Emperor Huai is later killed; Sima Rui takes the throne at Jiankang and Eastern Jin begins.
shots: The Luoyang palace scarred by the princes' wars
At Ningping over a hundred thousand Jin troops are surrounded by cavalry
Luoyang falls and the palaces burn
Emperor Huai flees and is captured
The gentry flee south across the river
liangjin.yongjia.title: The Yongjia Disaster: the Fall of Luoyang

liangjin.zhouchu.end: Zhou Chu reforms and becomes a loyal official, dying in battle at Liumo thirty years later.
shots: Hills and water of Yixing, the long bridge over the river
The elders sigh: three scourges remain
A white-browed beast on the southern hills
A flood dragon under the long bridge, surfacing and sinking for three days and nights
Hearing the villagers celebrate, he realises he was one of the scourges
liangjin.zhouchu.title: Ridding Three Scourges: Zhou Chu

liangjin.zuti.end: Zu Ti retakes Henan, but undermined by the court he dies of grief at Yongqiu, mourned like a father.
shots: Beacon smoke on the north bank of the river
In youth, two friends rise to sword-dance at a midnight cockcrow
A hundred households of followers; the boat reaches midstream
Camped at Huaiyin, he casts weapons in a forge
He strikes the oar and swears an oath
liangjin.zuti.title: Striking the Oar Midstream: Zu Ti's Northern Campaign

liaojin.abaoji.end: Bohai becomes the Dongdan kingdom; Abaoji dies on the way home, and Empress Shulü cuts off her right hand to place in his coffin.
shots: Tents of the eight Khitan tribes by the Huang River
The chiefs elect Abaoji as khagan
His brothers plot three times; Abaoji pursues them himself
At Longhua Abaoji proclaims himself Heavenly Emperor
Campaign east: Huhan city of Bohai surrenders
liaojin.abaoji.title: Founding the Khitan State: Yelü Abaoji

liaojin.caizhou.end: Aizong hangs himself and his successor dies within a day; Jin ends and the Song carry his remains south to their ancestral temple.
shots: Bianjing has fallen; Emperor Aizong flees south
Caizhou is small and short of grain
Song and Mongol armies, one south, one north
No grain inside, assaults outside
The Youlan pavilion
liaojin.caizhou.title: Caizhou: the Fall of Jin

liaojin.dading.end: Shizong's voice breaks as he sings of his ancestors; he dies four years later, remembered as a 'little Yao and Shun'.
shots: At Liaoyang the generals proclaim him emperor
Mourning Lady Wulinda, he never names another empress
Peace with Song; the two courts become uncle and nephew
The northern granaries fill in the Dading years
At a feast in Huining Shizong sings a Jurchen song himself
liaojin.dading.title: The Dading Reign: Emperor Shizong of Jin

liaojin.dashi.end: At Qatwan Sultan Sanjar is crushed and Western Liao dominates Central Asia for nearly ninety years until the Mongols arrive in 1218.
shots: In the Jia mountains the Liao emperor and the scholar-general argue
Two hundred horsemen slip away north by night
At Kedun the chiefs of seven prefectures and eighteen tribes gather
The army crosses the Tianshan with endless camel trains
On the Qatwan steppe Khitan cavalry strike from three sides
liaojin.dashi.title: Balasagun: Yelü Dashi Founds the Western Liao

liaojin.hubudagang.end: The Liao army is crushed; Aguda presses on, and within ten years Liao falls to Jin.
shots: Winter ice on the Huntong River
The Head-Fish Feast: the chiefs dance one by one
Ningjiang: two thousand five hundred horsemen rise
The Liao emperor leads his army in person, camps stretching for miles
Hubudagang
liaojin.hubudagang.title: Hubudagang: Aguda Rises in Revolt

liaojin.sanfeng.end: Chen Heshang dies defiant and the Mongols honour him with mare's milk; Jin loses its best troops and falls at Caizhou two years later.
shots: Outside Junzhou three peaks barely visible in the snow
A hundred and fifty thousand Jin soldiers trudge through the snow
Mongol horsemen circle the flanks, never engaging, never leaving
Three days of snow; soldiers freeze standing, weapons stuck to their hands
A captured general shouts his own name at the enemy tent
liaojin.sanfeng.title: Sanfeng Mountain: the Great Snow

liaojin.wushan.end: Hailing's own officers storm his tent and kill him; Jin withdraws, peace is renewed, and he is posthumously demoted to commoner.
shots: A painted screen of Lin'an's lakes and hills in the Yanjing palace
Jin armies march south by several routes
News from the east: Wanyan Yong has taken the throne
At Caishi the Jin crossing is beaten back
A rain of arrows at the temple by Guazhou ferry
liaojin.wushan.title: A Horse on Mount Wu: Prince Hailing's Southern Campaign

liaojin.xiaoguanyin.end: The empress is ordered to die and the musician's clan executed; two years later Yelü Yixin frames the crown prince too, and only under Tianzuo is the empress posthumously restored.
shots: Outside the great autumn hunting tent the emperor rides off in pursuit of game while the empress stands before the tent
In a lonely palace courtyard she holds her pipa and writes ten songs, "Return to the Heart Court"
A palace maid hands a page of erotic verse to the privy councillor
The emperor stares at the page: it is in the empress's own hand
A white silk cord hangs down and a pipa string snaps
liaojin.xiaoguanyin.title: The Ten Fragrances: Empress Xiao Guanyin

liaojin.xiaotaihou.end: After Chanyuan Song and Liao keep the peace; she hands power to Shengzong in 1009 and dies that year, credited with Liao's golden age.
shots: Emperor Jingzong dies at a travelling palace
The dowager weeps: a widowed mother and a young son
In 986 Song invades on three fronts
Yelü Xiuge crushes Cao Bin at Qigou Pass
The dowager rides south to Chanzhou in her war chariot
liaojin.xiaotaihou.title: Empress Dowager Chengtian: Xiao Chuo

liaojin.xixiawang.end: Western Xia ends and Genghis Khan dies that summer; the Xia ruler is executed and much of Tangut writing vanishes with the state.
shots: Mongol cavalry cross the Yellow River at several points
Lingwu falls and the generals scramble for loot
A scholar alone gathers books and medicinal herbs in the ruins
At the travelling palace below the Liupan mountains the Khan falls ill
The gates of Zhongxing open; the Xia ruler walks out holding a golden Buddha
liaojin.xixiawang.title: Nine Crossings of the Yellow River: the Fall of Western Xia

liaojin.yuanhao.end: Yuanhao founds the Great Xia; Song refuses recognition and three major battles follow, while the Tangut script survives into the Ming.
shots: A boy at the foot of the Helan mountains refuses brocade clothes
He shaves his own head and orders the whole country to follow within three days
Scholars break Chinese characters apart and recombine them stroke by stroke
A high platform is built south of Xingqing
He mounts the platform and reads a proclamation in the new script
liaojin.yuanhao.title: The Tangut Script: Yuanhao Declares Himself Emperor

ming.dali.end: 134 are jailed, over 180 flogged and more than ten die; Yang Shen, beaten twice, is exiled to Yongchang in Yunnan, and the emperor holds power for over forty years.
shots: A fifteen-year-old prince arrives from Anlu and refuses to enter the capital with the rites of a crown prince
For three years memorials pile up and the senior grand secretary resigns
By the Golden Water Bridge a Hanlin scholar cries out: to die for principle, today is the day
Over two hundred officials kneel weeping before the Zuoshun Gate, calling on the Founding Emperor and Emperor Xiaozong
Guards come out with lists and drag them away one by one, the beating of the court staves unceasing
ming.dali.title: The Zuoshun Gate: The Great Rites Controversy

ming.fangxiaoru.end: The prince has him dismembered in the market at forty-six, hundreds of his kin and friends die with him, and only in the Wanli years are the Jianwen martyrs rehabilitated.
shots: Fire lights up the palace in Nanjing and the Jianwen emperor vanishes
A scholar in mourning clothes is dragged into the hall, his weeping filling the steps
The Prince of Yan comes down the steps: sir, do not torment yourself, I only mean to be a Duke of Zhou to a young king
Paper and ink are set before him; he takes the brush and writes four great characters: the Yan bandit usurps the throne
He throws down the brush: if I die, I die, but this edict I will not write
ming.fangxiaoru.title: The Edict Will Not Be Written: Fang Xiaoru

ming.hairui.end: The emperor calls Hai Rui a Bigan but denies being King Zhou; when the emperor dies, Hai Rui weeps and vomits his prison meal, then is freed.
shots: Incense swirls in the Taoist halls of the Western Park
Hai Rui buys a coffin
The memorial is delivered to the Western Park
The emperor throws it down: seize him before he escapes
In the imperial prison Hai Rui hears the news
ming.hairui.title: The Memorial on Public Order: Hai Rui

ming.huweiyong.end: Hu Weiyong is executed and the chancellorship abolished forever; ten years later the purge widens and over thirty thousand are implicated.
shots: Memorials pile up at the Nanjing Secretariat
Champa envoys wait outside the palace gate unannounced
Taizu rebukes the ministers, who blame one another
Tu Jie denounces Hu Weiyong for treason
The Secretariat's signboard is taken down
ming.huweiyong.title: The Hu Weiyong Case: Abolishing the Chancellor

ming.jingnan.end: The Jianwen emperor vanishes; Zhu Di takes the throne as Yongle, and Fang Xiaoru is executed for refusing to write the edict.
shots: Beiping, the Prince of Yan's palace
The edict to reduce the princes arrives; the Prince of Yan rebels
On the walls of Jinan hangs Taizu's spirit tablet
The Jinchuan Gate opens
Fire in the palace
ming.jingnan.title: Jingnan: the Jinchuan Gate

ming.lishizhen.end: Li Shizhen dies in 1593 without seeing it printed; three years later the Compendium appears in Nanjing, the emperor merely notes "kept for reading", and the book spreads to Japan and Europe.
shots: In the hills of Qizhou a middle-aged physician with a herb basket crouches to study a white-flowered plant
He brews the flower into wine, drinks himself half-drunk and has someone laugh and dance beside him to see if he follows
In his study drafts pile to the rafters; he strikes out the old ones and rewrites for the third time
At the Yanshan Garden in Taicang he lays fifty-two scrolls before the leading man of letters and asks for a preface
With the last scroll finished he writes the title at the head
ming.lishizhen.title: The Compendium of Materia Medica: Li Shizhen

ming.liujin.end: The emperor orders Liu Jin put to death by slicing, the streets packed with onlookers, and his partisans are stripped of rank or die in prison.
shots: Officials kneel outside the Fengtian Gate in the blazing sun, waiting on a eunuch's judgement
In a Ningxia camp two men talk by lamplight; one traces the character "Jin" on the table
At the victory banquet Liu Jin leaves early and Zhang Yong draws a memorial from his sleeve
Late at night the emperor himself leads the raid on Liu Jin's house, gold and silver piled like hills
Two daggers are found hidden in his fan and the emperor roars: the slave really meant to rebel
ming.liujin.title: The Standing Emperor: The Fall of Liu Jin

ming.meishan.end: The Chongzhen emperor hangs himself on Coal Hill; Li Zicheng enters Beijing, and forty days later the Qing come through the pass.
shots: Beijing in the third month
The Shun army advances east from Xi'an
The bell is rung to summon the officials; no one comes
The city falls; the palace
A tree on Coal Hill
ming.meishan.title: Coal Hill: the Year 1644

ming.ningyuan.end: Nurhaci withdraws and dies that year; three years later Yuan races to defend Beijing, is jailed and executed by slicing in 1630.
shots: The lone fortress of Ningyuan with Western cannon on the walls
Gao Di orders all forts abandoned; Yuan Chonghuan refuses
Yuan Chonghuan writes an oath in his own blood
Later Jin troops dig at the walls; cannon fire rains down
Outside Beijing's Guangqu Gate, the Guan–Ning relief army
ming.ningyuan.title: Ningyuan: Yuan Chonghuan

ming.poyanghu.end: After more than thirty days Chen Youliang is killed by a stray arrow; Zhu Yuanzhang becomes King of Wu and founds the Ming four years later.
shots: Mist and waves stretch over Lake Poyang
Hongdu is besieged for over eighty days
Chen Youliang's giant ships lashed together in formation
Wind rises; seven small boats loaded with gunpowder and reeds
Fire attack
ming.poyanghu.title: Lake Poyang: the Decisive Battle of Zhu and Chen

ming.qijiajun.end: Nine victories at Taizhou end the pirate threat; Qi Jiguang writes his training manual, the New Treatise on Military Efficiency.
shots: Mountains, sea, bamboo groves and paddies of eastern Zhejiang
At Yiwu miners and farmers enlist
The mandarin-duck formation: bamboo spears, rattan shields, long spears
At Taizhou the pirates land
A blade in the bamboo grove
ming.qijiajun.title: The Qi Family Army: Victory at Taizhou

ming.qinliangyu.end: Back in Sichuan she resists Zhang Xianzhong, who dares not approach Shizhu; she dies past seventy, the only woman given her own biography for military merit in the dynastic histories.
shots: By the Hun River a Sichuan force with long white-staffed spears fights to the last as its commander falls
In the Shizhu chieftain's hall a woman general sets aside mourning white and puts on armour
The White Staff Army leaves Sichuan, crosses the Qinling and marches north
Below Yongping the spears stand thick and the Later Jin cavalry pulls back
On the terrace the emperor hands her a scroll of poems himself: robes of Shu brocade she cut herself
ming.qinliangyu.title: The White Staff Army Comes to the Rescue: Qin Liangyu

ming.saerhu.end: Within five days three Ming armies are destroyed with forty-five thousand dead, and the balance in Liaodong is reversed.
shots: At the Shenyang command, a map of the four-pronged advance
Du Song crosses the Hun River in snow
Below Sarhu the Later Jin cavalry close in
At Shangjianya Ma Lin's camp collapses
At Abudali ridge Liu Ting fights to the death
ming.saerhu.title: Sarhu: Four Armies Lost

ming.tangyin.end: Scorning the clerkship, Tang Yin lives by selling paintings in his Peach Blossom Dock studio, carving a seal "Nanjing Laureate", and whether the case was unjust is still debated.
shots: The Nanjing examination list is posted, a Suzhou man's name at the top
The next year a great boat carries two graduates north to the capital in luxury
Right after the metropolitan exam rumours sweep the capital: someone had the questions in advance
In the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison the provincial laureate is chained and interrogated
Released and demoted to a petty clerk in Zhejiang, he turns and walks back to Suzhou
ming.tangyin.title: The Examination Scandal: Tang Yin

ming.tingji.end: The case is closed as the work of a madman; five years later the prince reigns a single month before dying after the red pill, and the Three Cases feed a decade of factional strife.
shots: At dusk a man with a jujube-wood club bursts through the Ciqing Palace gate and fells the old eunuch on guard
He fights his way to the eaves of the front hall before the attendants bring him down
In the Ministry of Justice prison an official sets a bowl of rice before the prisoner: tell the truth and you eat
The prisoner names two eunuchs, both serving in Consort Zheng's palace
The emperor who has not seen his ministers in twenty-five years takes the crown prince's hand in the Cining Palace: this boy is most filial and I love him dearly
ming.tingji.title: The Club Attack Case: The Ciqing Palace

ming.tumubao.end: Esen fails after five days and withdraws; the captive emperor returns, regains the throne eight years later, and has Yu Qian executed.
shots: Autumn beyond Juyong Pass
Half a million men rush north
At Tumu wells are dug but find no water
Beijing debates fleeing south; Yu Qian objects fiercely
Cannon fire outside the Desheng Gate
ming.tumubao.title: Tumu and the Defence of Beijing: Yu Qian

ming.wanggongchang.end: Relief silver is handed out while Wei Zhongxian keeps crushing opponents; a year later the emperor dies, and whether gunpowder, earthquake or meteor caused the blast is still unknown.
shots: On the morning of the sixth day of the fifth month the Wanggong gunpowder works in southwest Beijing lies silent
With a huge blast a black cloud shoots skyward like a giant lingzhi mushroom
For miles around houses are flattened and tiles, people and beasts are flung into the air
In the Qianqing Palace the emperor drops his bowl and runs for the Jiaotai Hall; an attendant beside him is struck by a falling tile
As the dust settles an edict of self-reproach issues from the palace
ming.wanggongchang.title: The Tianqi Explosion: Disaster at the Wanggong Works

ming.wangyangming.end: The prince is captured within forty-odd days; to avoid the emperor's farce of recapturing him, Wang hands the prisoner to the eunuch Zhang Yong.
shots: On the Fengcheng road Wang Shouren hears of the revolt and turns back
At Ji'an, forged proclamations and phantom troops
The prince's fleet sails down the Yangtze to besiege Anqing
Government troops seize the undefended Nanchang
On Lake Poyang fire attacks the prince's linked ships
ming.wangyangming.title: Defeating the Prince of Ning: Wang Shouren

ming.weizhongxian.end: Wei Zhongxian hangs himself at Fucheng and Madam Ke is flogged to death; Chongzhen has the corpse dismembered and punishes over two hundred eunuch partisans, yet the Ming falls seventeen years later.
shots: In living shrines across the land wooden statues wear python robes as officials line up to kneel and hail the Nine-Thousand-Year Lord
By lamplight the Vice Censor-in-Chief writes his memorial, listing twenty-four great crimes one by one
In the imperial prison sacks of earth press on him and iron nails are driven into his ears
Under his pillow lies a letter in blood: laugh, laugh, and laugh again
Three years later in an inn at Fucheng an old eunuch listens to a ditty outside the window and unties his sash
ming.weizhongxian.title: Lord of Nine Thousand Years: Wei Zhongxian and the Donglin

ming.xuguangqi.end: Ricci dies in Beijing in 1610 and the emperor grants him a burial ground; Xu Guangqi rises to grand secretary, compiles the Chongzhen calendar and the Complete Treatise on Agriculture, and the last nine books wait 250 years for Li Shanlan and Wylie.
shots: Inside Xuanwu Gate in Beijing a long-nosed Westerner holds a thick book while the Hanlin scholar opposite writes it down
The paper fills with points, lines and circles beside the new words they coin: point, line, surface, parallel, right angle
In the palace a Western chiming clock strikes as the emperor and eunuchs crowd round
The first six books are done; Ricci wants to go on, but the scholar decides to print first
In his preface he writes: in a hundred years everyone will study this
ming.xuguangqi.title: Euclid's Elements: Xu Guangqi and Matteo Ricci

ming.xukexia.end: Xu Xiake builds a stupa for Jingwen, travels on to Tengchong, revises the Mount Jizu gazetteer for Mu Zeng in Lijiang, and is carried home by litter when his feet fail, dying the next year.
shots: At his door in Jiangyin a man of fifty and a monk shoulder their packs and board a small westbound boat
Moored on the Xiang River at night, bandits leap aboard and in the firelight the monk refuses to let go of his sutras
In a Nanning temple the dying monk hands him a sutra written in blood: take me to Mount Jizu
Carrying the monk's ashes he crosses the high mountains of Guangxi and Guizhou
On the summit of Mount Jizu he lays down the ashes and sutra as the morning bell rings
ming.xukexia.title: The Great Journey West: Xu Xiake

ming.yangjisheng.end: Yang Jisheng dies at forty mourned by the realm; seven years later Yan Song falls, his son is beheaded and he starves, and Yang's couplet "iron shoulders bear the Way" endures.
shots: After three days of fasting a War Ministry official writes by lamplight: Yan Song has ten great crimes
The memorial reaches the West Park and the chief grand secretary murmurs in the emperor's ear
After a hundred strokes of the staff, the prisoner cuts the rotting flesh from his leg with a shard of bowl
His wife kneels outside the palace gate holding a petition to die in her husband's place
At the western execution ground he recites his last poem: noble spirit returns to the void, a loyal heart shines for ages
ming.yangjisheng.title: Iron Shoulders Bear the Way: Yang Jisheng

ming.yuanchonghuan.end: After eight months in prison Yuan Chonghuan is dismembered in the western market, childless and dispossessed; only when the Qing compiled the Ming History from its own archives was the ruse revealed.
shots: North of the Great Wall the Later Jin cavalry swings round through the Mongol steppe and bursts in at Da'ankou
The commander rides day and night with nine thousand horsemen to reach the walls of Beijing
Outside the Guangqu Gate he fights in armour bristling with arrows
In the Later Jin camp two officers deliberately whisper outside the tent of a captured eunuch
At the audience on the terrace the emperor gives the word and guards strip the commander's cap on the spot
ming.yuanchonghuan.title: The Jisi Incursion: The Death of Yuan Chonghuan

ming.zhangjuzheng.end: The treasury fills for ten years; within two years of his death his family is stripped of everything and his reforms undone until he is rehabilitated in the 1620s.
shots: In the Wenhua Hall, a ten-year-old emperor and his tutor
Performance ledgers in triplicate, checked monthly
News of his father's death: the mourning-leave controversy
Land resurvey: surveyors measure the fields
The Single Whip tax spreads across the realm
ming.zhangjuzheng.title: The Wanli Reforms: Zhang Juzheng

ming.zhenghe.end: Zheng He makes seven voyages to over thirty countries as far as East Africa, at great cost; after the Xuande reign the voyages stop.
shots: Sixty-two great ships at Liujiahe in Suzhou
The fleet sails past Champa and Java
Night battle at Palembang; Chen Zuyi is captured
At Ceylon Zheng He leads two thousand men straight to the royal city
Envoys from Bengal present a 'qilin'
ming.zhenghe.title: Seven Voyages: Zheng He

ming.zhuyuanzhang.end: Guo Zixing, struck by his looks, unties him himself and makes him a bodyguard, later marrying him to his adopted daughter Lady Ma; sixteen years later he proclaims the Ming at Yingtian.
shots: Drought grips Huaibei, the fields nothing but cracked earth, and a youth kneels before three fresh graves
He shaves his head and sweeps floors, burns incense and strikes the bell at the Huangjue Temple
The temple runs out of grain; alms bowl in hand he walks alone along the roads of western Huai
A letter reaches the temple: his fellow villager Tang He urges him to join the army at Haozhou
At the Haozhou gate the guards tie up the monk and prepare to behead him as a spy
ming.zhuyuanzhang.title: Monk of the Huangjue Temple: Zhu Yuanzhang Joins the Army

nanbeichao.changchou.end: Wei thinks the Song well supplied and fears an ambush; Tan Daoji returns intact, but is later executed: you destroy your own Great Wall!
shots: Song camps along the Ji River
The grain carts are empty; soldiers pour the last rice into the measure
A deserter runs to the Wei camp at night
Torches blaze; someone calls out the measures, but it is sand
At dawn the Song army marches out slowly in full armour
nanbeichao.changchou.title: Counting Sand as Grain: Tan Daoji

nanbeichao.chenqingzhi.end: Chen Qingzhi shaves his head as a monk and escapes home, where Emperor Wu still enfeoffs him.
shots: Seven thousand white-robed horsemen cross the Huai
Below Xingyang Northern Wei armies surround them
The white robes scale the wall and take it in one charge
A new ballad spreads through Luoyang
A flash flood below Mount Song scatters the white robes
nanbeichao.chenqingzhi.title: Armies Avoid the White Robes: Chen Qingzhi

nanbeichao.cuihao.end: Moved by his candour the emperor spares Gao Yun; Cui Hao is executed and the Cui of Qinghe with their in-law clans are wiped out, and two years later the emperor is murdered by the eunuch Zong Ai.
shots: In the palace at Pingcheng the emperor hands charge of the history to a white-haired Han adviser
In the archives hundreds of clerks copy out the old deeds of the Tuoba ancestors character by character
Beside the road east of the suburban altar a forest of steles stands, carved with the state history
At the palace gate the crown prince holds his teacher's sleeve and tells him what to say to the emperor
In the great hall Gao Yun kneels and tells the truth sentence by sentence
nanbeichao.cuihao.title: The State History Case: Cui Hao

nanbeichao.damo.end: Emperor Wu returns to the palace; he gives himself to the temple four times and later starves in the Hou Jing rebellion.
shots: The pagoda of Tongtai Temple towers north of Jiankang
The emperor removes his crown and puts on monk's robes
At Yongning Temple in Luoyang a foreign monk praises the golden spire
In a cave on Mount Song a man sits facing the wall
On the river a single reed carries a man north
nanbeichao.damo.title: Giving Himself to Tongtai Temple: Emperor Wu of Liang and Bodhidharma

nanbeichao.fanzhen.end: Fan likens body and spirit to a blade and its sharpness; when Xiao Yan becomes Emperor Wu of Liang he orders over sixty nobles to refute the essay, and Fan still will not yield.
shots: At the Western Residence below Jilong Hill princes, scholars and famous monks sit amid curling incense
The Prince of Jingling asks: if you deny karma, why are some born rich and others poor?
Fan Zhen points out of the window: blossoms on one branch fall in the wind, some onto mats, some into the cesspit
Wang Rong calls in private: drop this essay and the post of Secretariat Gentleman is yours
Fan Zhen laughs and writes: while the body lasts the spirit lasts; when the body perishes the spirit perishes
nanbeichao.fanzhen.title: On the Mortality of the Soul: Fan Zhen

nanbeichao.heyin.end: Over a thousand, perhaps two thousand, officials die and the court is all but emptied; two years later Emperor Xiaozhuang stabs Erzhu Rong in the Mingguang Hall, and Northern Wei soon splits east and west.
shots: Outside Jinyang the black banners of the Jie cavalry blot out half the sky, come to avenge the dead emperor
At a Yellow River ferry the newly chosen emperor slips across from Luoyang to Erzhu Rong's camp
The empress dowager, head shaved, kneels pleading before his horse, and Erzhu Rong rises and turns away
The muddy waves of the Yellow River swallow the empress dowager and the three-year-old boy emperor
Outside the travelling palace at Heyin the princes and officials line up to greet the emperor, and cavalry suddenly close in from all sides
nanbeichao.heyin.title: The Heyin Massacre: Erzhu Rong

nanbeichao.houjing.end: Taicheng falls and Emperor Wu starves; Hou Jing is killed in 552, leaving Jiangnan in ruins.
shots: Jiankang, Taicheng and the Yangtze
Hou Jing rebels at Shouyang
Crossing at Caishi with boats from inside collaborators
Taicheng besieged; Yang Kan defends it
The city falls
nanbeichao.houjing.title: Taicheng: the Hou Jing Rebellion

nanbeichao.lanling.end: The soldiers compose the Prince of Lanling song; his remark 'family matter' arouses the emperor's suspicion, and he is forced to drink poison.
shots: Below Mangshan the Zhou camps stretch to the walls of Luoyang
Five hundred horsemen form up in the snow
The cavalry charge into the Zhou lines, out, and back in
Below Jinyong the defenders cannot recognise the masked general
He removes his helmet and shows his face
nanbeichao.lanling.title: Prince of Lanling Enters the Battle: Mangshan

nanbeichao.lidaoyuan.end: Li Daoyuan is killed with his brother and two sons; Xiao Baoyin proclaims himself emperor and soon falls, while the Commentary on the Waterways becomes one of China's great works of geography.
shots: By the Yellow River an official rides upstream, his attendants carrying bundles of bamboo slips and maps
At the source of a stream he crouches and asks an old shepherd the water's ancient name
In the capital he seizes a prince's favourite and, as the prince begs the empress dowager for pardon, has the man killed first
In Guanzhong the post station stands on a mound with its well below, and rebels ring the mound
Standing before the station he glares at the closing rebels and shouts them down
nanbeichao.lidaoyuan.title: Commentary on the Waterways: The Death of Li Daoyuan

nanbeichao.mulan.end: Home at last, she dresses her hair at the window; her comrades are amazed—twelve years together and they never knew Mulan was a woman.
shots: Click-clack, Mulan weaves at the door
Twelve scrolls of conscription, each with her father's name
A horse from the east market, a saddle from the west
Leaving at dawn, camping by the Yellow River at dusk
Ten thousand li to war, flying over passes and mountains
nanbeichao.mulan.title: The Ballad of Mulan

nanbeichao.xiaowen.end: The capital moves to Luoyang in 494; the royal clan takes the surname Yuan, and the crown prince who resisted is deposed.
shots: Wind and sand of the north at Pingcheng
The army marches south, ostensibly against Qi
Endless autumn rain at Luoyang
Ministers kowtow before his horse
Changing dress and language
nanbeichao.xiaowen.title: Moving the Capital to Luoyang: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei

nanbeichao.yuanjia.end: Wei fails at Xuyi and withdraws, leaving scorched land; swallows return to nest in trees, and the Yuanjia prosperity fades.
shots: Autumn waters between the Yangtze and the Huai
Emperor Wen reads Wang Xuanmo's plans and dreams of Langjuxu
Huatai resists all assaults
Wei crosses the river and Wang Xuanmo flees
On Mount Guabu the Wei emperor gazes at the Yangtze
nanbeichao.yuanjia.title: The Hasty Yuanjia Campaign

nanbeichao.yubi.end: After fifty days seventy thousand Eastern Wei dead lie in one mound; Gao Huan falls ill and withdraws.
shots: The lone fortress of Yubi north of the Fen River
An earthen ramp rises south of the city; wooden towers are lashed on the walls
In the tunnels, firewood and bellows
Cloth screens hang wherever the siege engines strike
The Chile plain below the Yin mountains
nanbeichao.yubi.title: The Battle of Yubi: Wei Xiaokuan

nanbeichao.zuchongzhi.end: The emperor dies before the calendar is adopted; it takes effect in 510 at his son's urging, and his south-pointing carriage outperforms its rival.
shots: Under the night sky, a gnomon and a bundle of counting rods
Around the winter solstice he records the shadow length day by day
At court Dai Faxing rises angrily
He divides the circle into more and more sides on paper
In the Leyou park two south-pointing carriages turn together
nanbeichao.zuchongzhi.title: The Daming Calendar: Zu Chongzhi

nansong.caishi.end: The Jin crossing fails with heavy losses; Prince Hailing turns to Yangzhou and is killed by his own officers, and Southern Song is saved.
shots: Caishi, one of the narrowest points of the Yangtze
Scattered soldiers sit by the road, saddles off
Yu Yunwen rallies the commanders with appeals to loyalty
Paddle-wheel ships ram the small Jin boats
Thunderclap bombs burst on the water
nansong.caishi.title: Caishi Cliff: Yu Yunwen

nansong.diaoyucheng.end: Möngke dies at Diaoyu and the Mongols withdraw; the fortress holds for twenty years and surrenders only after the Song falls.
shots: Hezhou, where three rivers meet
The Ran brothers propose a chain of mountain forts
Möngke leads the siege himself
Summer night, stones from the catapults
Death of the Great Khan
nansong.diaoyucheng.title: Diaoyu Fortress: Where the Scourge of God Broke His Whip

nansong.ehu.end: The meeting ends without a winner; six years later Zhu Xi invites Lu to lecture at White Deer Grotto and has his words carved in stone, and their split becomes the divide between Principle and Mind learning.
shots: At the foot of Goose Lake Hill several sedan chairs stop before the gate of an old temple
In the lecture hall scholars of two schools sit facing each other across a long table
Lu Jiuling recites a poem first and Lu Jiuyuan answers: the work of ease and simplicity lasts and grows great
Hearing the line "fragmented labours drift and sink" Zhu Xi's face changes
After three days of argument no one has convinced anyone and the chairs outside the gate disperse one by one
nansong.ehu.title: The Goose Lake Meeting: Zhu Xi and Lu Jiuyuan

nansong.huangtiandang.end: Fire arrows break the Song fleet and Wuzhu escapes north, but Jin never again crosses the river lightly.
shots: The river at Zhenjiang between Jinshan and Jiaoshan
Han Shizhong's tall seagoing ships block the river
Lady Liang beats the war drum herself
Overnight the Jin army digs a thirty-li canal to the Qinhuai
On a windless day fire arrows strike the ships' sails
nansong.huangtiandang.title: Huangtiandang: Han Shizhong and Lady Liang

nansong.jiasidao.end: Jia Sidao is banished and killed on the road by his escort; a year later the Yuan enter Lin'an.
shots: Mongol armies besiege Ezhou; boats crisscross the river
An envoy slips across to the enemy camp by small boat
At Banxian Hall on West Lake men lie on the floor fighting crickets
Five years of siege at Xiangyang; urgent reports pile up unopened
At Dingjiazhou 130,000 Song troops scatter without fighting
nansong.jiasidao.title: Banxian Hall: Jia Sidao

nansong.kaixi.end: Shi Miyuan takes power; in 1208 Han's coffin is opened and his head sent to the Jin in a box to buy the Jiading peace, and Shi rules alone for over twenty years.
shots: At court in Lin'an an edict for the northern campaign is read and the whole hall cheers
On the Huai the Song take a few small towns, then are routed below Suzhou
In a Sichuan headquarters a general accepts the seal of King of Shu sent by the Jin
In the palace the empress and a vice minister confer in low voices over a note the emperor never signed
On the road to court at dawn guards of the Palace Command stop the chief minister's chair and hustle him into the Yujin Garden
nansong.kaixi.title: The Head in a Box: The Kaixi Campaign and Han Tuozhou

nansong.liqingzhao.end: In her afterword she reflects that what is gathered must scatter; she edits and presents the thirty-chapter Records on Metal and Stone.
shots: In the Guilai Hall at Qingzhou the couple sit among books making tea
Fifteen carts of books head south
By the river at Chiyang her husband rides off, turning to give instructions
Alone she guards a few chests of books, drifting from town to town
By lamplight she opens his manuscript and writes the afterword
nansong.liqingzhao.title: Records on Metal and Stone: Li Qingzhao

nansong.luyou.end: Sixty years after Lu You's death the Southern Song falls with the Central Plains never recovered, and Lin Jingxi writes: your descendants see the realm united, but how will they tell you at the altar?
shots: On the Board of Rites list Lu You's name stands near the top until the chief minister's red brush strikes it out
Outside the camp at Nanzheng autumn wind sweeps Dasan Pass as a poet in iron armour rides the frontier
In the snow he braces a long spear and faces down a tiger
In the old house at Shanyin a white-haired man listens to the night storm and dreams of armoured horses on frozen rivers
On his deathbed he asks his sons for brush and paper and writes his last poem
nansong.luyou.title: Do Not Forget to Tell Me at the Family Altar: Lu You

nansong.songci.end: The five-scroll book becomes the forensic standard of the Yuan, Ming and Qing and is translated into Korean, Japanese and European languages; Song Ci dies in office at Guangzhou two years later.
shots: In the judicial commissioner's hall backlogged files are piled like hills as Song Ci reads them one by one
In roadside grass lies a body with a dozen wounds, yet nothing has been taken
Song Ci has the villagers bring every sickle in their homes and lay them out under the blazing sun
Flies come one by one and settle on a single sickle
Song Ci lifts that sickle and its owner falls to his knees
nansong.songci.title: Collected Cases of Injustice Rectified: Song Ci

nansong.xiangyang.end: After Fancheng falls, Lü Wenhuan surrenders Xiangyang in 1273; with the Yangtze gate open, the Yuan reach Lin'an three years later.
shots: Xiangyang and Fancheng face each other across the Han
Yuan troops build forts and palisades ring upon ring
Zhang Shun and Zhang Gui's boats charge the blockade at night
Muslim trebuchet stones fall on Fancheng
Lü Wenhuan climbs the wall and looks south
nansong.xiangyang.title: The Battle of Xiangfan: Lü Wenhuan

nansong.xinqiji.end: Xin Qiji seizes Zhang Anguo amid fifty thousand men and has him executed at Jiankang.
shots: Geng Jing's rebel camp in Shandong
Yiduan steals the seal and flees; Xin Qiji rides after him alone
At Jiankang Emperor Gaozong receives Xin Qiji
Terrible news from Haizhou: Geng Jing is dead
In the Jin camp Zhang Anguo is drinking
nansong.xinqiji.title: Fifty Horsemen: Xin Qiji

nansong.yashan.end: Lu Xiufu leaps into the sea with the emperor and Song ends; four years later Wen Tianxiang is executed in Dadu.
shots: Twin hills of the Yamen strait on the South China Sea
Over a thousand ships lashed into a line
Yuan cuts off the water supply; the people on board drink seawater
On a Yuan warship Wen Tianxiang is forced to watch
Carrying the boy emperor into the sea
nansong.yashan.title: Yashan: Wen Tianxiang

nansong.yuefei.end: The recovered land is lost again; Yue Fei is framed and executed, and Qin Hui answers Han Shizhong: perhaps there was something.
shots: The lost heartland south of the Yellow River
Jin breaks the treaty and marches south
Yancheng: the linked cavalry
Twelve golden tablets in a single day
Withdrawal
nansong.yuefei.title: Loyal to the End: Yue Fei

nansong.zongze.end: Zong Ze dies reciting Du Fu and crying 'cross the river'; his successor undoes his work and Kaifeng is soon lost.
shots: After Jingkang, Kaifeng's walls are broken and its streets empty
A white-haired old man rides alone into the volunteers' camp
At the execution ground a young officer is about to be beheaded
The old man writes his twentieth-odd petition urging the emperor to return
On his sickbed he cries out three times: cross the river
nansong.zongze.title: Cross the River: Zong Ze

qin.baishe.end: The elders of Pei kill the magistrate and open the gates to Liu Ji, now Lord of Pei, with two or three thousand local men.
shots: In the great marsh west of Feng reeds sway in the dark
The precinct chief cuts the convicts' ropes
On the marsh path a great serpent blocks the way
In the Mangdang hills people find him by following a cloud
A silk letter is shot onto the walls of Pei
qin.baishe.title: Killing the Serpent at Pei: Liu Ji

qin.bolangsha.end: The mace hits a decoy; the furious emperor orders a ten-day search, and Zhang Liang changes his name and hides at Xiapi.
shots: Yellow sand on the road outside Yangwu
A young man and a giant crouch behind a dune
The emperor's procession approaches in great pomp
An iron mace flies and smashes a carriage
It is not the emperor's carriage
qin.bolangsha.title: The Strike at Bolangsha: Zhang Liang

qin.changcheng.end: The northern walls join into one line and the southern supply route opens; three new commanderies are founded at great human cost.
shots: Beacon towers along the ridges of the northern mountains
Meng Tian leads three hundred thousand men to build walls along the terrain
Between southern ranges two rivers flow apart
Shi Lu surveys the water and cuts a canal joining the Xiang and the Li
The locks open and grain boats cross the ridge southward
qin.changcheng.title: The Great Wall and the Lingqu Canal

qin.dazexiang.end: Chen Sheng reaches Chen and declares himself king of Zhangchu; the whole realm rises.
shots: Rain without end at Dazexiang
Nine hundred conscripts, the roads impassable
A silk message inside a fish belly
Night: a bonfire at the shrine, a fox cries
Clubs cut from trees, poles raised as banners
qin.dazexiang.title: Are Kings and Nobles Born to It? Dazexiang

qin.fengshan.end: The emperor grants the pine the fifth noble rank and sacrifices at Liangfu; the dismissed scholars mock his soaking in private.
shots: A road built from the foot of Mount Tai to the summit
Seventy scholars argue below the mountain about the ancient rites
The imperial carriage climbs the new road
A stele is raised on the summit praising Qin's virtue
On the way down a sudden storm; he shelters under a pine
qin.fengshan.title: Sacrifice on Mount Tai: the Fifth-Rank Pine

qin.fenshu.end: Next year over four hundred scholars are buried at Xianyang; Fusu protests and is sent north, and Fu Sheng's books lie hidden in the wall for years.
shots: At a palace banquet seventy academicians come forward to toast
Chunyu Yue steps out urging the emperor to follow antiquity
Li Si unrolls his memorial and reads it point by point
Bamboo slips piled into mountains in county squares
An old academician hides a scroll inside a wall
qin.fenshu.title: Burning the Books: Officials as Teachers

qin.julu.end: Wang Li is captured; the allied generals crawl on their knees into Xiang Yu's camp, and Zhang Han soon surrenders.
shots: The Zhang River outside Julu
Song Yi feasts while the soldiers freeze and starve
At the morning council Xiang Yu beheads Song Yi
Crossing the river: boats sunk, cauldrons smashed, huts burned
Nine battles, cutting the walled supply road
qin.julu.title: Breaking the Cauldrons, Sinking the Boats: Julu

qin.shaqiu.end: Those who said 'deer' are quietly destroyed; soon Zhao Gao forces the Second Emperor to kill himself and Qin is near its end.
shots: The eastern tour crosses endless plains
At the Shaqiu terrace the carriage is silent
Zhao Gao, Li Si and Huhai: a single edict
In Shang commandery, Fusu receives the edict
In the court, a deer
qin.shaqiu.title: Shaqiu: Calling a Deer a Horse

qin.shuwen.end: The empire is divided into thirty-six commanderies, small seal script becomes standard, and weights and measures are unified.
shots: The six states fall; a long scroll unrolls
Xianyang palace: ministers debate the imperial title
Court debate: commanderies or fiefs
Each of the six states writes differently, one word in many forms
One script for the realm
qin.shuwen.title: One Script for All: the First Emperor

qin.xufu.end: The emperor kills the fish, falls ill at Pingyuan ford and dies at Shaqiu; the Shiji mentions Xu Fu's fate only once more.
shots: Below Langya Terrace the Eastern Sea stretches endlessly
Xu Fu memorialises about three sacred mountains in the sea
Thousands of boys and girls board the ships
Nine years later the alchemists claim a giant fish blocked them
At Zhifu a repeating crossbow kills a huge fish
qin.xufu.title: Xu Fu Sails East in Search of Immortals

qing.aobai.end: Thirty charges are laid; Kangxi spares Oboi's life but imprisons him, and the teenage emperor takes real control of the government.
shots: Fourteen-year-old emperor at court in the Qianqing Palace
Oboi argues fiercely before the throne, sleeves rolled up
Suksaha is sentenced to strangulation
Young palace guards practise wrestling
Oboi comes for an audience and is seized on the spot
qing.aobai.title: Seizing Oboi: the Young Kangxi

qing.duodi.end: Yinzhen becomes the Yongzheng emperor; his rivals die in confinement, and he publishes a defence of his succession and creates the secret heir system.
shots: At a frontier camp the crown prince is deposed
Princes form factions and officials take sides
In the north-west camp, Great General Yinti
At Changchun Garden Kangxi is dying
Longkodo reads the last will
qing.duodi.title: Nine Princes Fight for the Throne: Yongzheng's Succession

qing.gengzi.end: The court reaches Xi'an; the Boxer Protocol is signed with eleven powers for an indemnity of 450 million taels, Li Hongzhang dies two months later, and on their return the court posthumously raises Consort Zhen.
shots: In Beijing red-turbaned Boxers pour into the streets and church roofs go up in flames
Behind the legation walls on Dongjiaomin Lane foreign soldiers block doors and windows with sandbags
Before dawn the empress dowager pins up her hair in a plain bun, changes into summer clothes and boards a common mule cart with the emperor
By a well in the palace a eunuch leads a frail young woman away
Outside the Desheng Gate the cart has barely left when white flags cover the city wall
qing.gengzi.title: The Boxer Year: The Court Flees West

qing.hongloumeng.end: Cao Xueqin dies poor around a New Year's Eve with the book unfinished; the eighty chapters circulate in manuscript until Cheng Weiyuan and Gao E print a 120-chapter edition in 1791, and who wrote the last forty is still debated.
shots: The gate of the Nanjing textile commission is sealed and the whole household boards carts heading north
In thatched huts below the Western Hills a middle-aged man spreads manuscript paper on a broken table
A friend visits; he buys wine on credit and talks of the old splendour beside the Qinhuai River
In the margins of the manuscript someone has filled every space with notes in red
At the start of the book he writes four lines: pages of absurd words, a handful of bitter tears
qing.hongloumeng.title: Pages of Absurd Words: Cao Xueqin

qing.humen.end: The destruction lasts over twenty days; the Opium War breaks out the next year.
shots: Foreign merchant ships at the Pearl River mouth
The imperial commissioner arrives in Guangdong
Confiscation: chest after chest
Pools are dug on the Humen beach
Lime goes into the pools and smoke rises
qing.humen.title: Destroying Opium at Humen: Lin Zexu

qing.jiawu.end: The Zhiyuan sinks; Deng Shichang refuses rescue and dies with over two hundred men, and the Treaty of Shimonoseki follows the next year.
shots: The Yellow Sea off Dadonggou
The Beiyang fleet forms its line
Japanese ships circle, guns blazing
The Zhiyuan lists
Full speed ahead
qing.jiawu.title: The Battle of the Yellow Sea: Zhiyuan

qing.keju.end: That winter the Ministry of Education is founded and thirteen centuries of exams end; thousands of old-style scholars lose their path, some to schools, some abroad, some like Liu Dapeng keeping an empty village school.
shots: In the Jiangnan examination hall over twenty thousand cells stretch in long rows, each just big enough for one man
An old candidate lights a candle in his cell and writes an eight-legged essay stroke by stroke
In a governor-general's office several ministers sign a memorial: while the exams last, the schools cannot rise
On a new school's sports ground students in short jackets follow their instructor in drill
In a Shanxi village a tutor closes his diary; the pupils outside the window have all gone
qing.keju.title: The End of the Exams: A Hall Used for Thirteen Centuries

qing.malgaerni.end: The embassy leaves empty-handed by way of Canton; four decades later British ships return with guns, and the boy who took the purse is among the MPs who back the war.
shots: Off Dagu a Western warship under full sail rides at anchor, its holds full of gifts
