The carts carrying the gifts fly small flags reading "Tribute envoy of England"
Outside the tent hall at Rehe the ministers argue for days over whether to kneel
Inside, the emperor in his eighties unties a purse from his belt and hands it to a twelve-year-old boy
An edict is written: the Celestial Empire abounds in all things and lacks nothing
qing.malgaerni.title: The Celestial Empire Lacks Nothing: The Macartney Embassy

qing.nibuchu.end: The Treaty of Nerchinsk is China's first border treaty with a Western state; the next year boundary stones in five scripts are raised, and the eastern frontier stays largely quiet for over a century.
shots: By the Amur, Qing troops ring the fort of Albazin as those inside dig cellars in the snow
An embassy rides north across the steppe, two robed Western missionaries among its ranks
Outside Nerchinsk two tents stand side by side, each guarded by the same number of soldiers
The envoys cannot understand each other, so the missionaries carry every word across in Latin
The treaty is written in Manchu, Russian and Latin, and both sides seal it together
qing.nibuchu.title: Nerchinsk: Albazin and the Border Treaty

qing.qianlong.end: Jiaqing lists twenty crimes and orders Heshen to kill himself; folk sayings exaggerate his fortune, which official history does not quantify.
shots: The imperial barge sails south on the Grand Canal
Inspecting the sea wall at Haining
At the Grand Council Heshen monopolises the memorials
At the Siku Quanshu office Ji Yun edits books
Five days after the retired emperor dies, Heshen is arrested
qing.qianlong.title: Southern Tours and Heshen: the Qianlong Era

qing.qiujin.end: Qiu Jin is executed at Xuanting Crossing in Shaoxing at dawn, barely past thirty; the next year Wu Zhiying and Xu Zihua risk their safety to bury her beside the Xiling Bridge on West Lake.
shots: On a Japanese quay a Chinese woman in kimono with a short sword at her side steps off the boat
On the Datong school ground she rides and teaches the students to shoot
News comes from Anqing that Xu Xilin's assassination has failed and his heart has been cut out
Troops surround the school; she does not leave but sits inside waiting for them
On the interrogation paper she writes just seven characters: autumn wind, autumn rain, sorrow beyond bearing
qing.qiujin.title: Autumn Wind, Autumn Rain: Qiu Jin, Heroine of Jianhu

qing.sanfan.end: In 1689 China and Russia sign the Treaty of Nerchinsk fixing the eastern border.
shots: The young emperor in the Forbidden City
The order to abolish the feudatories; Wu Sangui rebels
Eight hard years until Yunnan is pacified
At Penghu Shi Lang leads the fleet
Albazin on the Amur
qing.sanfan.title: The Three Feudatories, Taiwan and Albazin: Kangxi

qing.shanhaiguan.end: The Shun army breaks and retreats west; in the fifth month Qing enters Beijing and soon makes it the capital.
shots: Shanhai Pass, where the Great Wall meets the sea
News of Beijing's fall reaches the pass
The Shun army comes from the west; the Qing army comes south
At Yipianshi the two armies clash
A gale whips up sand; Qing cavalry burst out
qing.shanhaiguan.title: Shanhai Pass: Yipianshi

qing.shunzhi.end: Shunzhi dies at twenty-four; Xuanye becomes the Kangxi emperor under four regents, and the will lists over ten self-criticisms.
shots: The imperial consort's chamber in the Chengqian Palace
Consort Donggo dies and the emperor suspends court for five days
Shunzhi posthumously names her empress
In the Yangxin Hall the emperor has smallpox
Wang Xi drafts the last edict beside the bed
qing.shunzhi.title: The Death of Consort Donggo: the Shunzhi Emperor

qing.taiping.end: Hong Xiuquan dies weeks before the city falls; Li Xiucheng escorts the young heir out, is captured, writes his confession and is executed.
shots: At Jintian in Guiping the God Worshippers gather
The Taiping army sails down the Yangtze and takes Jiangning
Princes' palaces inside the Heavenly Capital
Xiang Army fleets battle the Taiping on the Yangtze
A tunnel mine blows open the walls of Tianjing
qing.taiping.title: Tianjing: the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom

qing.wenziyu.end: Yongzheng spares Zeng Jing while Lü Liuliang's corpse is exhumed and mutilated; within two months of his death Qianlong has Zeng and Zhang executed and the book withdrawn, so the emperor's defence becomes a banned book.
shots: In Xi'an a scholar stops the governor-general's sedan chair and hands up a letter
The letter urges him to rise against the Qing, calling him a descendant of Yue Fei
In a secret room the governor and the scholar burn incense and swear an oath, and the scholar finally names his teacher
In the Forbidden City the emperor rebuts the scholar's charges one by one in his own hand
A book is printed and sent to every school in the empire for scholars to read
qing.wenziyu.title: Awakening from Delusion: The Zeng Jing Case

qing.wuchang.end: Province after province joins; the Republic of China is founded on New Year's Day 1912, the emperor abdicates on 12 February, and two thousand years of monarchy end.
shots: An autumn night in Wuchang
The Hankou safehouse is exposed and the member list seized
Gunfire from the engineering battalion
The Chuwangtai arsenal
The eighteen-star flag is raised
qing.wuchang.title: The Wuchang Uprising: the Abdication

qing.wuxu.end: The Six Gentlemen are beheaded at Caishikou; apart from the Imperial University almost every reform is cancelled.
shots: The road between the Summer Palace and the Forbidden City
Reform edicts one after another
At Fahua Temple Tan Sitong visits Yuan Shikai at night
Cixi returns to the palace and resumes power
Caishikou: six men are executed
qing.wuxu.title: 1898: the Hundred Days' Reform

qing.xinyou.end: Sushun is seized at Miyun and beheaded at Caishikou, Zaiyuan and Duanhua ordered to kill themselves; the era name becomes Tongzhi and Empress Dowager Cixi holds power for nearly half a century.
shots: At the sickbed in the Rehe palace eight ministers kneel in a row to hear the emperor's last words
Two young empresses dowager sit behind a screen, each holding a seal
Prince Gong arrives from Beijing for the mourning and confers in secret with the empress dowager
In autumn rain the emperor's coffin moves slowly along the mountain road while the empresses' carriages take a shortcut ahead
In Beijing the palace gate shuts and a eunuch reading the edict names three ministers
qing.xinyou.title: Ruling from Behind the Screen: The Xinyou Coup

qing.yangnaiwu.end: Ge Pinlian died of illness, not poison; Yang Naiwu and Bi Xiugu are freed, magistrate Liu Xitong is exiled to Heilongjiang and many Zhejiang officials are dismissed, while Yang returns to silkworms and Bi becomes a nun.
shots: In a small town in Yuhang a young tofu-shop worker dies suddenly with bloody fluid at his mouth
In the county hall the ankle press tightens and a scholar finally nods
A woman with a bundle on her back walks a thousand miles to petition in Beijing
In a Shanghai newspaper office typesetters set the case into the paper issue after issue
At Haihui Temple the coffin is opened and the coroner's silver needle stays bright
qing.yangnaiwu.title: Yang Naiwu and Little Cabbage: The Strangest Case of the Late Qing

qing.yangzhou.end: Shi Kefa dies defiant before Dodo; ten days of massacre follow, and his clothes are buried at Plum Blossom Ridge.
shots: The walls of Yangzhou below Plum Blossom Ridge
Dodo's letter demanding surrender reaches the walls
The letter is left unopened
Qing cannon pound the north-west corner
The city falls; Shi Kefa tries to cut his throat and survives
qing.yangzhou.title: Yangzhou: Shi Kefa

qing.yuanmingyuan.end: Under the Convention of Peking Tianjin is opened, part of Kowloon ceded and the indemnity raised; Xianfeng dies at Rehe the next year without returning, and the ruins suffer further plunder.
shots: Pavilions mirror in the lakes of the Yuanmingyuan and the fountains of the Western Mansions still play
Before dawn the imperial carriage hurries out of the north gate, bound for Rehe
Allied soldiers storm the garden and strip it of porcelain, paintings and jewels
Thick smoke covers the sky west of Beijing as the fire burns for three days and nights
Prince Gong signs in the hall of the Board of Rites while the sky outside is still grey
qing.yuanmingyuan.title: Garden of Gardens: The Burning of the Yuanmingyuan

qing.zengguofan.end: Zeng rebuilds the army and takes Wuchang that autumn, but Shi Dakai beats him again at Hukou and Jiujiang; the Xiang Army fights on for over a decade before taking Tianjing in 1864.
shots: On the Xiang River a civil official drills a band of farmer-soldiers at the oars
On the river at Jinggang the Xiang Army's boats are scattered by the wind as Taiping craft sweep downstream
Zeng Guofan stands at the bow watching his fleet break, leaps into the river, and an aide plunges in after him
Almost at once news of victory comes from Xiangtan, where Taqibu routs the Taiping
Back in Changsha he writes four words in his memorial: defeated again, fighting again
qing.zengguofan.title: Defeated Again, Fighting Again: Zeng Guofan and the Xiang Army

qing.zhengchenggong.end: After a nine-month siege Coyett surrenders and the Dutch leave Taiwan; Zheng Chenggong dies that same year.
shots: Wind and waves in the Taiwan Strait
Warships set out from Jinmen
Luermen: shallow water and sandbars
A spring tide rises and the fleet passes through
Cannon fire below Fort Zeelandia
qing.zhengchenggong.title: Zheng Chenggong Takes Taiwan: Luermen

qing.zhennanguan.end: The French are routed and Lang Son retaken; the French cabinet falls, yet Qing signs a peace treaty—'defeated without losing'.
shots: The burned gate of Zhennan Pass
A long wall is built at the pass
French artillery pounds the wall
Feng Zicai leaps over the wall, spear in hand
Pursuing the enemy to Lang Son
qing.zhennanguan.title: Zhennan Pass: Feng Zicai

qing.zuozongtang.end: Zuo's march backs Zeng Jize's talks in St Petersburg; the 1881 treaty recovers most of Ili, Xinjiang becomes a province in 1884, and Zuo dies in Fuzhou the next year.
shots: At court two factions argue endlessly over the coast and the frontier
Along the Hexi Corridor column after column of soldiers farm as they advance west
Below the Tianshan Liu Jintang's army rides through the night and the cities of the south open their gates
Outside Suzhou a black-lacquered coffin is lifted onto a cart behind the army
A man of sixty-eight on horseback looks back once at Jiayu Pass
qing.zuozongtang.title: With a Coffin Beyond the Pass: Zuo Zongtang Recovers Xinjiang

sanguo.baima.end: Cao Cao forbids pursuit — each serves his own lord — and Guan Yu returns to Liu Bei, keeping the title Marquis of Hanshou ever after.
shots: Outside Baima the Yuan camps stretch on, a general's canopy raised in their midst
A lone rider bursts from Cao's lines, a long blade trailing low
Amid ten thousand soldiers a blade flashes and the canopy falls
In Cao's camp the gifts are sealed one by one beside a letter of farewell
On the long road a single rider heads north while Cao Cao watches from afar and sends no pursuit
sanguo.baima.title: Beheading Yan Liang amid Ten Thousand: Guan Yu Leaves Cao

sanguo.caochong.end: Cao Cao is delighted and does it at once; the kind and gifted boy dies at thirteen in 208, and Cao Cao tells Cao Pi: my misfortune is your good fortune.
shots: The great elephant sent from the east stands in the courtyard, taller than the eaves
The ministers argue around it; none can think how to weigh it
A child of five or six tugs his father's sleeve: I know a way
The elephant is led onto a boat, the hull sinks, and the boy cuts a mark at the waterline
The elephant is led off, baskets of stone are loaded until the boat sinks to the same mark
sanguo.caochong.title: Cao Chong Weighs the Elephant: A Precocious Child

sanguo.caomao.end: Cao Mao dies at twenty; Sima Zhao blames Cheng Ji and exterminates his clan, Wang Jing dies with his mother for refusing to inform, and Cao Huan is enthroned, abdicating to Sima Yan five years later.
shots: On the Lingyun Terrace the twenty-year-old emperor calls three ministers before him and produces an edict
He throws the edict down: Sima Zhao's intentions are known to every passer-by
On a rainy night the emperor draws his sword, mounts his carriage and charges out of the palace with a few hundred servants and guards
Below the southern gate Jia Chong tells Cheng Ji: Lord Sima has fed you for just this day
A long halberd runs through the man in the carriage
sanguo.caomao.title: Known to Every Passer-by: The Duke of Gaogui Village

sanguo.changban.end: Liu Bei joins Guan Yu's fleet and Liu Qi at Xiakou; having met Lu Su at Dangyang, the Sun–Liu alliance begins.
shots: At Changban near Dangyang a hundred thousand civilians follow the army south
Cao's elite cavalry ride three hundred li in a day and night
Zhao Yun carries the infant through the chaos
Zhang Fei holds the broken bridge, glaring, spear levelled
No enemy dares come near
sanguo.changban.title: Changban: Zhao Yun and Zhang Fei

sanguo.chibi.end: Many of Cao's men burn or drown and he retreats north; Sun and Liu take parts of Jing and the three-way division takes shape.
shots: The great river flows east past the Red Cliffs
At Chaisang Sun Quan cuts his desk with his sword
Cao's warships linked bow to stern
Huang Gai's fire ships ride a fierce south-east wind
Fierce fire, fierce wind
sanguo.chibi.title: The Battle of Red Cliffs: Fire on the Fleet

sanguo.dandao.end: Guan Yu sends the man away; soon Cao Cao takes Hanzhong, and Liu Bei splits Jing province with Sun Quan along the Xiang River.
shots: Two armies face each other on the river at Yiyang
Each side keeps its troops a hundred paces back
The generals meet bearing only their swords
Lu Su reproaches Guan Yu; a man in the audience cuts in
Guan Yu rises, blade in hand
sanguo.dandao.title: The Single-Sword Meeting: Lu Su and Guan Yu

sanguo.dingjunshan.end: Xiahou Yuan falls and the Wei army breaks; Cao Cao comes to contest Hanzhong, utters "chicken ribs" and withdraws, and in July Liu Bei proclaims himself King of Hanzhong.
shots: On the hills south of the Mian River in the Hanzhong basin, Liu Bei's camp rises overnight
At night Shu troops set fire to the abatis outside the Wei camp
The Wei commander leads four hundred men out to repair the abatis himself
On the summit Fa Zheng raises his hand: now we can strike
The old general charges downhill amid thundering drums and gongs, his blade falling on the men at the abatis
sanguo.dingjunshan.title: Mount Dingjun: Huang Zhong Slays Xiahou Yuan

sanguo.dongzhuo.end: Lü Bu spears Dong Zhuo and Chang'an celebrates, but two months later Li Jue and Guo Si take the city and Wang Yun is killed.
shots: Weiyang Palace in Chang'an, the emperor just recovered
Dong Zhuo loses his temper and hurls a halberd at Lü Bu
Wang Yun meets Lü Bu in secret
Li Su and a dozen men in guard uniforms wait at the north gate
By imperial edict, strike the traitor
sanguo.dongzhuo.title: The Chain Stratagem: Killing Dong Zhuo

sanguo.gaopingling.end: Cao Shuang surrenders and his clan is executed; Wei takes Shu, Jin replaces Wei, and Jin conquers Wu in 280.
shots: Luoyang in the first month
The Grand Tutor lies ill, speaking confusedly
Cao Shuang escorts the emperor out to the tombs
The city gates close; the floating bridge over the Luo
Thirty years later surrender flags at Stone City
sanguo.gaopingling.title: The Gaopingling Coup: the Three Kingdoms End in Jin

sanguo.guandu.end: The Wuchao stores burn, Zhang He defects and Yuan's army collapses; Yuan Shao dies two years later.
shots: South of the Yellow River the ramparts at Guandu face each other
Months of stalemate; Cao's grain runs low
Xu You defects to Cao's camp at night
Five thousand men, each with a bundle of firewood, march by night
Fire at Wuchao
sanguo.guandu.title: The Battle of Guandu: Night Raid on Wuchao

sanguo.hefei.end: Sun Quan's horse clears the bridge; Ling Tong fights on north of it until his men all fall, then swims back wounded, and Cao Cao names Zhang Liao General Who Conquers the East.
shots: On the walls of Hefei a wooden box is opened: Cao Cao's order says if Sun Quan comes, Zhang and Li go out to fight
At night oxen are slaughtered in the city and eight hundred men eat their fill
At dawn Zhang Liao in armour charges the Wu lines with his halberd, shouting his own name
Sun Quan retreats onto a high mound, guarding himself with a long halberd, watching eight hundred men cut through a hundred thousand
The bridge at Xiaoyao Ford is broken for more than ten feet; a fine horse leaps the gap
sanguo.hefei.title: Terror at Xiaoyao Ford: Eight Hundred Against a Hundred Thousand

sanguo.huatuo.end: Cao Cao's headaches persist; when his beloved son Cao Chong lies dying he laments, I regret killing Hua Tuo, and the physician's book is lost, with only his disciples passing on fragments.
shots: The chancellor clutches his head in a migraine as the physician slips a needle into his back
The physician shows his disciple the moves of tiger, deer, bear, ape and bird
The physician on leave at home stays away; a messenger presses at the gate
In the Xu prison he holds out a scroll to the jailer, who draws back his hand
He asks for fire and drops the book into the flames
sanguo.huatuo.title: The Death of Hua Tuo: The Lost Book of Medicine

sanguo.jieting.end: With no foothold, Zhuge Liang withdraws to Hanzhong, executes Ma Su and demotes himself three ranks.
shots: Mountains of Longyou and the vital road at Jieting
Ma Su abandons the water and climbs the hill
Zhang He cuts off their water supply
Wang Ping beats the drums and holds firm; Wei suspects an ambush
Ma Su is executed to answer to the army
sanguo.jieting.title: Jieting and the Empty City: Ma Su

sanguo.kongrong.end: Kong Rong and his family are executed at fifty-six; his friend weeps over the body unpunished, and Cao Pi later collects his writings, ranking him first of the Seven Masters of Jian'an.
shots: Kong Rong's hall is full of guests; he raises his cup: the seats always full, the cups never empty, what have I to worry about
In the chancellor's office a scroll of charges lies open on the desk
Constables burst into the Kong house while two children are still playing chess in the courtyard
Kong Rong turns: let the guilt end with me; can the two children be spared
The child rises calmly: have you ever seen whole eggs beneath an overturned nest
sanguo.kongrong.title: Beneath an Overturned Nest: The Death of Kong Rong

sanguo.lesi.end: Liu Shan lives seven peaceful years in Luoyang and dies in 271; some call him a fool, others a clever pretender, and "too happy to miss Shu" becomes an idiom.
shots: At a banquet in the Prince of Jin's mansion in Luoyang the music and dances of Shu begin
The former Shu ministers bow their heads and weep; only the Duke of Anle laughs happily
The Prince of Jin asks: do you miss Shu
He sets down his cup: it is pleasant here, I do not miss Shu
The Prince of Jin turns to Jia Chong: can a man be so heartless
sanguo.lesi.title: Happy Here: Not Missing Shu

sanguo.longzhong.end: Zhuge Liang leaves to serve Liu Bei, and the three-way division becomes Shu Han's grand strategy.
shots: A thatched cottage in the Longzhong hills
Xu Shu says: Zhuge Kongming is a sleeping dragon
Through wind and snow, the second visit finds no one
Sitting face to face, a map unrolls
The realm in three
sanguo.longzhong.title: Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage: the Longzhong Plan

sanguo.menghuo.end: Nanzhong is pacified; local chiefs keep their posts, no garrison is left, and Meng Huo later becomes a court censor.
shots: Miasma over the forests of Nanzhong
Ma Su sees him off: win their hearts
Crossing the Lu River into the barren lands
Meng Huo is captured, shown the camp and released
The seventh time: you are Heaven's own might
sanguo.menghuo.title: Seven Captures of Meng Huo: Pacifying the South

sanguo.qibu.end: Cao Pi is ashamed; Cao Zhi, moved from fief to fief and never employed, dies at forty-one as Prince of Chen, ranked by Zhong Rong among the highest poets.
shots: On the Bronze Sparrow Terrace in Ye a youth writes a rhapsody in one stroke, astonishing the guests
Years later in the hall the emperor says coldly: make a poem within seven steps or be executed
He takes the first step, then the second
At the fifth and sixth steps he begins: beans are boiled to make a broth
The seventh step lands: born of the same root, why such haste to scorch each other
sanguo.qibu.title: The Seven-Step Poem: Cao Zhi

sanguo.qijun.end: In the twelfth month Guan Yu and his son are captured and executed, and all of Jing passes to Wu.
shots: Fancheng stands isolated on the Han River
Autumn rains; the Han overflows
Yu Jin's seven armies are drowned; Pang De stands on the dike
Lü Meng hides troops in boats rowed by men in white
Maicheng: an isolated town surrounded
sanguo.qijun.title: Flooding the Seven Armies, Retreat to Maicheng

sanguo.shouchan.end: Emperor Xian becomes Duke of Shanyang, allowed the Han calendar and rites in his fief; he outlives Cao Pi by eight years, and Fanyang is renamed Fanchang.
shots: In the palace at Xuchang an envoy comes a third time to demand the imperial seal
The empress calls the envoy in, rebukes him point by point, and throws the seal down the steps
At Fanyang a three-tiered altar rises, officials, the Xiongnu chanyu and envoys of the four quarters in ranks
The new king ascends, receives the seal and ribbon, and burns firewood in offering to Heaven
Descending after the rite he turns and says: now I understand what happened with Shun and Yu
sanguo.shouchan.title: The Abdication Terrace: Han Falls, Wei Rises

sanguo.sunce.end: Sun Quan succeeds with Zhang Zhao leading the officials and Zhou Yu hurrying back for the funeral; Sun Quan will hold the east for more than fifty years and found the state of Wu.
shots: In the western hills of Dantu a swift horse leaves the escort far behind
Three figures rise in the woods holding bows
An arrow strikes the young general in the cheek
At his sickbed he hands the seal and ribbon to his nineteen-year-old brother
The seal passes into Sun Quan's hands and behind the screen a lamp goes out
sanguo.sunce.title: Death of the Little Conqueror: Sun Ce Ambushed

sanguo.wuzhangyuan.end: Sima Yi retreats; people say a dead Zhuge put a living Zhongda to flight, and Sima Yi calls him the genius of the age.
shots: Wuzhang Plains south of the Wei River
Soldiers farm alongside the local people by the Wei
Women's clothing is sent to Sima Yi, who refuses battle
Autumn night, lamps in the camp
Banners turn and drums beat as if to attack Sima Yi
sanguo.wuzhangyuan.title: Autumn Wind at Wuzhang Plains: the Falling Star

sanguo.yanglu.end: Lu Kang dies in 274 and Yang Hu in 278, naming Du Yu his successor; the people of Xiangyang raise the Stele of Tears, and when Wu falls two years later the emperor weeps: this is Grand Tutor Yang's achievement.
shots: On the Jing border the Jin general wears a light fur and loose sash instead of armour, with barely a dozen guards
A jar of wine is sent across to the Wu camp and its commander drinks without hesitation
Lu Kang falls ill; Yang Hu sends medicine and the Wu officers try to stop him drinking
Lu Kang lifts the bowl: would Yang Hu poison anyone
Years later a stele rises on Mount Xian and everyone who looks at it weeps
sanguo.yanglu.title: The Friendship of Yang and Lu: Would Yang Hu Poison a Man

sanguo.yiling.end: The Shu army collapses and Liu Bei retreats to Baidi, dying the next year after entrusting his son to Zhuge Liang.
shots: Shu camps stretch hundreds of li along the Three Gorges roads
Liu Bei marches east
Lu Xun holds fast while his generals grumble
In midsummer the Shu camps move into the forest
Each man carries a bundle of reeds; fire attack
sanguo.yiling.title: Burning the Linked Camps: the Battle of Yiling

sanguo.yinping.end: Liu Shan surrenders and Shu Han ends after forty-three years; Deng Ai is falsely accused and killed on the way to prison, and Zhong Hui soon dies in his own failed revolt.
shots: The cliffs of Jiange stand like a gate, Shu banners crowd the pass and the Wei army halts below
On the Yinping trail a Wei column cuts through the mountain and hangs plank roads on the cliffs
The cliff is too steep; the commander wraps himself in felt and rolls down
Outside Mianzhu Zhuge Liang's son forms his line and dies in battle
At the north gate of Chengdu the emperor, hands bound, a coffin carried behind him, comes out to surrender
sanguo.yinping.title: Crossing Yinping in Secret: Deng Ai Enters Shu

sanguo.zhujiu.end: Thunder happens to roll and Liu Bei blames his start on it; soon he leaves Xu to intercept Yuan Shu, kills Che Zhou in Xu Province, and the girdle-edict plotters are executed.
shots: In a back garden in Xu a man bends over a vegetable bed, watering
In a pavilion green plums and a pot of wine are set out, and the Minister of Works invites him to sit
Cao Cao counts them off one by one: Yuan Shu, Yuan Shao, Liu Biao, Sun Ce — none of them count
He looks at Liu Bei: the only heroes in the realm today are you and I
The chopsticks fall and a thunderclap splits the sky
sanguo.zhujiu.title: Talking of Heroes over Wine: The Heroes of the Age

shang.bigan.end: King Zhou cuts out Bigan's heart; Jizi feigns madness and is jailed; the court musicians flee to Zhou, and soon King Wu attacks.
shots: At a palace feast, a pair of ivory chopsticks
Jizi looks at the chopsticks and sighs deeply
Weizi leaves the city at night and looks back once
Bigan kneels below the steps for three days and will not rise
King Zhou stands: I hear a sage's heart has seven openings
shang.bigan.title: Three Good Men of Yin: Bigan

shang.fuhao.end: Fu Hao returns victorious and leads sacrifices; she dies before King Wu Ding, who divines for her in the afterlife.
shots: Outside the Yin capital, the Huan River and distant hills
A diviner scorches a turtle shell; cracks spread across the bone
Fu Hao takes command; three thousand troops and ten thousand more assemble
Marching west against the Qiang, chariots raise dust
A great bronze axe swings
shang.fuhao.title: Fu Hao, Woman General

shang.muye.end: King Zhou burns himself on the Deer Tower; King Wu enters Shang and Zhou takes the realm.
shots: Shang outskirts: distant hills and the Deer Tower in morning mist
At Mengjin the lords join forces and cross the river
At dawn on the jiazi day King Wu addresses the army at Muye
The Shang host is huge but turns its weapons around
Fire rises at the Deer Tower
shang.muye.title: Muye: King Wu Defeats King Zhou

shang.pangeng.end: The people settle in the new city and the Shang way revives.
shots: The old capital north of the river, its walls decaying
Pangeng addresses the court, citing the former kings
The people gather, sighing and complaining
Crossing the river: boats linked end to end
Yin: the new city completed on the bank of the Huan River
shang.pangeng.title: Pangeng Moves to Yin

shang.tangdao.end: Tang reforms the calendar and colours of state; the institutions of Shang are founded.
shots: In the wild a net is spread on all four sides
Tang orders three sides removed, leaving only one
At Bo the lords stand below the steps to hear his decree
Great drought; the fields crack and nothing grows for five years
In the mulberry grove he cuts off his own hair
shang.tangdao.title: Open the Net on Three Sides: Tang Prays at the Mulberry Grove

shang.tonggong.end: Yi Yin returns the government; Taijia reforms, the lords return, and he is honoured as Taizong.
shots: Palaces of Bo with a smear of distant hills
Tang dies; Wai Bing and Zhong Ren reign briefly in turn
Taijia takes the throne and ignores Tang's laws
Yi Yin sends Taijia to Tong Palace beside Tang's tomb
Three years later Yi Yin leads the officials to bring him back
shang.tonggong.title: Tong Palace: Yi Yin Exiles Taijia

shang.youli.end: King Zhou pardons the Lord of the West and grants him bow, arrows and axes; Wen asks him to abolish the burning pillar.
shots: Outside Zhaoge, the walls of Youli
In a cell an old man arranges yarrow stalks into hexagrams
The Zhou search far and wide for beauties, fine horses and rare treasures
The gifts reach King Zhou through Fei Zhong
King Zhou laughs: this one alone is enough to free him
shang.youli.title: Youli: the Lord of the West Imprisoned

shanggu.dayu.end: The nine provinces are settled, and Shun recommends Yu to Heaven as his heir.
shots: Floodwaters reach the sky; distant hills sink beneath the water
Gun dams the water with earth for nine years and fails
Yu takes up his father's task with level, line, compass and square, marking the mountains
Three times he passes his own door without entering: a stroke at the gate, and he turns away
He dredges the nine rivers and the water returns to the sea
shanggu.dayu.title: Thrice Past His Door: Yu Tames the Flood

shanggu.fuxi.end: The trigrams are drawn and fishing nets are knotted; later tradition credits all of it to Fuxi, though scholars doubt one man made them.
shots: Low clouds over the Thunder Marsh
A man stands on high ground gazing at the stars
He looks down at the earth, criss-crossed by tracks of birds and beasts
Early people try to catch fish by hand at the water's edge and keep missing
He draws one unbroken and one broken line on the ground
shanggu.fuxi.title: The Eight Trigrams: Fuxi

shanggu.hundun.end: The brush is in hand; the historian keeps to the old texts, and the next scroll begins with the Yellow Emperor.
shots: Blank paper; a single drop of ink falls and slowly spreads
A human figure rises from the ink, arms pushing sky and earth apart
The clear rises to become heaven, the murky sinks to become earth
A corner of the sky is broken, endless floods; Nüwa smelts stones
She patches the sky with five-coloured stones, closed in one stroke
shanggu.hundun.title: Opening of Chaos: Pangu and Nüwa

shanggu.shanrang.end: Homage, lawsuits and songs all turn to Shun; saying it is Heaven's will, he takes the throne.
shots: The plain of Pingyang, a thin line of distant hills
Yao asks the Four Peaks: who can succeed me?
Two daughters marry at the Gui River; Shun ploughs at Mount Li
Sent into the great forest, Shun walks through wind, thunder and rain
The chieftains' carriages pass Danzhu by and go to Shun
shanggu.shanrang.title: Abdication: from Yao to Shun

shanggu.shennong.end: Ploughs to teach the world and markets at midday are credited to Shennong by later Confucian tradition, not contemporary record.
shots: Waist-high wild grass along both banks of the Jiang River
He sharpens a piece of hardwood and drives it into the soil
Hills covered in plants, some edible, some poisonous
At noon people gather in a clearing carrying goods to trade
He bites a leaf and his face suddenly changes
shanggu.shennong.title: Tasting a Hundred Herbs: Shennong

shanggu.xihe.end: The calendar is fixed and all works prosper; the Canon of Yao counts it as Yao's first achievement.
shots: On the eastern shore the sun rises from the water
A man sets up a gnomon and records the sunrise direction
In a western valley another man sees the sun set
Bamboo slips filled with days: three hundred and sixty-six
On the horizon a second sun suddenly rises
shanggu.xihe.title: Ordering the Sun and Moon: Xihe and Yi

shanggu.zhuolu.end: With Chiyou taken, the chieftains honour Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong.
shots: The paper fades in; distant hills and open plains are drawn stroke by stroke
Xuanyuan cultivates virtue and trains troops; the chieftains rally to him
Three battles at Banquan: two great banners charge each other
Zhuolu: thick fog over the field, Chiyou's army within it
Chiyou is captured and killed: the banner falls and the fog lifts
shanggu.zhuolu.title: Zhuolu: the Yellow Emperor against Chiyou

sui.gaogouli.end: Of 305,000 who crossed the Liao, only 2,700 return; revolts follow and by the third campaign the empire is in chaos.
shots: A million troops on both sides of the Liao River
Nine armies cross, each man carrying a hundred days of grain
Eulji Mundeok enters the camp feigning surrender
Seven victories in one day, drawn deep to the Salsu River
Halfway across the Salsu the rear collapses first
sui.gaogouli.title: Three Campaigns Against Goguryeo: Disaster at the Salsu

sui.hongfu.end: Li Yuan admires his words and Li Shimin pleads for him; Li Jing later conquers the south and the Turks and becomes Duke of Wei.
shots: Turkic beacons flicker beyond Mayi commandery
The deputy prefect chains himself and rides south in a prison cart
Roads cut outside Chang'an, he is trapped in the city
Tang troops enter and a blade is at his throat
He shouts, and the Prince of Qin turns around
sui.hongfu.title: Chained Petition: Li Jing and Hongfu

sui.jiangdu.end: Emperor Yang is strangled at fifty and buried in a makeshift coffin; Yuwen Huaji marches north and Li Yuan proclaims Tang that May.
shots: Nightly music in the Jiangdu palace
The emperor looks in the mirror and says something to the empress
In the guards' barracks homesick soldiers whisper in small groups
At midnight the palace gate is opened from inside
At dawn Empress Xiao and the maids make a small coffin from bed boards
sui.jiangdu.title: The Jiangdu Coup: 'A Fine Neck'

sui.miechen.end: The last Chen emperor is pulled from a well with his consorts; nearly three centuries of division end.
shots: The two banks of the Yangtze face each other
Sui troops line the river, rotating garrisons to confuse Chen
New Year's Day 589, thick fog on the river
Han Qinhu crosses at Caishi by night
In the well of Jingyang Hall
sui.miechen.title: Crossing the River: Sui Conquers Chen

sui.shouchan.end: Yang Jian takes the throne in 581 and names his dynasty Sui; eight years later Sui crosses the Yangtze and reunites the realm.
shots: In the Zhou palace curtains hang low over Emperor Xuan's coffin
Two ministers carry an edict to Yang Jian's mansion
Outside Xiangzhou, Yuchi Jiong's army faces Wei Xiaokuan
His wife sends word: riding a tiger, you cannot dismount
In Linguang Hall the nine-year-old emperor hands over the seal
sui.shouchan.title: Abdication at Linguang Hall: Yang Jian Replaces Zhou

sui.wagang.end: Li Mi kills Zhai Rang, is beaten by Wang Shichong at Mangshan in 618 and surrenders to Tang; the Wagang men scatter.
shots: Wagang stronghold on the wasteland by the canal
Zhai Rang gathers followers and Li Mi joins him
Dahai Temple: ambush in the woods
Xingluo granary: the stores are thrown open
Rebels rise everywhere
sui.wagang.title: Wagang: Rebels Rise Everywhere

sui.yangguang.end: Emperor Wen dies in 604; the Zizhi Tongjian records rumours of forged edicts, while the official annals say only that he died.
shots: In the Prince of Jin's house instruments gather dust, strings broken
The crown prince's palace blazes with lights and concubines
The empress summons Yang Su for a whispered talk behind curtains
The crown prince is led out and stripped of rank
In Dabao Hall at Renshou Palace the curtain around the sickbed is pulled back
sui.yangguang.title: Renshou Palace: Yang Guang Seizes the Succession

sui.yanmen.end: Princess Yicheng warns of trouble in the north and relief armies arrive; the siege lifts, but the emperor breaks his promised rewards.
shots: Turkic horsemen cover the hills beyond Yanmen Pass
Thirty-nine of forty-one towns have fallen; arrows land before the throne
Minister Xiao Yu advises: send an envoy to Princess Yicheng
A boy tells the general: more banners by day, gongs and drums by night
In the Turkic camp the khagan receives an urgent letter from the north
sui.yanmen.title: The Siege of Yanmen: Phantom Army

sui.yunhe.end: The canal links north and south for a millennium of grain transport, but at the time women were drafted and the realm was in turmoil.
shots: Central plains between the Yellow River and the Huai
Over a million men and women dig the Tongji canal
Dragon boats four decks high, forty-five feet tall
The Yongji canal runs north to Zhuo commandery
A thousand-li canal joined end to end
sui.yunhe.title: The Grand Canal: Tongji and Yongji

sui.zhaozhou.end: The Anji Bridge, known as the Zhaozhou Bridge, is one of the oldest open-spandrel stone arch bridges in the world and still stands.
shots: The Xiao River floods and the wooden ferry bridge is swept away
Li Chun draws a very shallow arc on the riverbank
Twenty-eight stone arches are laid side by side like bows
Four small openings in the spandrels let floodwater pass
Fourteen hundred years later the bridge still stands
sui.zhaozhou.title: The Great Stone Bridge: Li Chun

tang.anshi.end: Lady Yang is strangled before the shrine; Xuanzong flees to Shu, the crown prince takes the throne at Lingwu, and the war drags on seven years.
shots: Huaqing Palace near Chang'an
War drums from Fanyang
Tong Pass falls
At Mawei Station the six armies refuse to march
Before the Buddhist hall
tang.anshi.title: War Drums from Yuyang: the An Lushan Rebellion and Mawei

tang.baijuyi.end: Bai Juyi spends nearly four years at Jiangzhou, building a cottage below Incense Burner Peak on Mount Lu, then moves on to Zhongzhou and ends his days in Luoyang as the Layman of Xiangshan.
shots: In Chang'an's Jing'an ward before dawn a chief minister is cut down by assassins on his way to court
A month later a small boat drifts east down the Yangtze carrying the banished official
On an autumn night at Penpu, among maple leaves and reeds, the host sees off a guest and hears a pipa from the next boat
After many calls a woman comes out, pipa half hiding her face, and plays with lowered eyes
The song ends with one stroke across all four strings like tearing silk, and the one who weeps most is the Sima of Jiangzhou
tang.baijuyi.title: The Pipa at Xunyang: Bai Juyi

tang.caizhou.end: By dawn the army is inside; Wu Yuanji is captured and executed, Huaixi is pacified and the Hebei governors tremble.
shots: Three years of war on the Huaixi plain
Li Su unties the captured Li You
At midnight they leave Zhangchai village in a blizzard
Geese and ducks on the pond are beaten to cover the army's noise
At the fourth drum they reach Caizhou and the gate opens
tang.caizhou.title: Into Caizhou on a Snowy Night: Li Su

tang.daluosi.end: Gao Xianzhi returns to Anxi and is later executed at Tongguan on a false charge; Du Huan lives among the Abbasids for over ten years, returns by sea to Guangzhou in 762 and writes one of the earliest Chinese eyewitness accounts of the Arab world.
shots: On the steppe west of the Pamirs thirty thousand Tang troops march more than seven hundred li
Below the walls of Talas the Tang and Abbasid armies face each other for five days
At night the Karluk troops within the Tang ranks suddenly turn their blades
The routed army jams the mountain pass; a general swinging a great club clears a road through men and horses
A captured Tang soldier looks back east as he is marched toward western cities
tang.daluosi.title: Talas: Gao Xianzhi's Western Campaign

tang.direnjie.end: Wu Zetian spares the seven and demotes Di Renjie to Pengze; later chief minister again, he persuades her to recall the Prince of Luling, and men say all the peaches and plums of the realm grow at his gate.
shots: In the interrogation bureau inside the Lijing gate few who enter come out alive
The chief minister confesses at once: the Zhou has renewed all things, an old Tang servant accepts death, the treason is true
At night he tears silk from his quilt, writes out the injustice and sews it into a padded coat
His son unpicks the coat his father sent home and the silk letter falls out
The empress asks why he confessed; he answers: had I not, I would already be dead under the lash
tang.direnjie.title: A Plea Written on Silk: Di Renjie

tang.dufu.end: Along this road Du Fu writes the Three Officers and Three Partings; that autumn he quits office and heads west into Shu, building a thatched cottage by the Huanhua stream in Chengdu.
shots: At dusk a gaunt middle-aged man walks into Shihao village and knocks at a door
At midnight fists pound the gate; the old man vaults the back wall and the old woman goes out to answer
The officer roars and the old woman weeps: my three sons went to Ye, two are already dead
She says: old as I am, let me go with you to Heyang, I can still cook the army's breakfast
At dawn as he sets out, only the old man stands at the gate to see him off
tang.dufu.title: Night Conscription at Shihao: Du Fu

tang.guoziyi.end: The Uighurs renew their alliance and together they crush Tibet at Lingtai; a disaster for Guanzhong is averted.
shots: Uighur and Tibetan camps outside Jingyang
Guo Xi grabs his father's reins in protest
He rides out of the gate with a few horsemen
He removes helmet and armour, throws down his spear and advances
The Uighur chieftains dismount and bow around him
tang.guoziyi.title: Facing the Uighurs Alone: Guo Ziyi

tang.hanyu.end: Han Yu spends eight months in Chaozhou opening schools, freeing bondservants and driving off crocodiles, so the river and hill there bear his name; the next emperor recalls him as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
shots: In Chang'an the Buddha bone is carried into the palace; nobles and commoners rush to give alms, some burning their scalps and arms
By lamplight the Vice Minister of Justice writes his memorial: the Buddha was a barbarian
The emperor reads it, flings it down and demands the writer's death
That same day he is escorted out of Chang'an heading south
At Lan Pass in heavy snow the horse can go no further, and his grandnephew catches up from behind
tang.hanyu.title: Remonstrating against the Buddha Relic: Banished to Chaozhou

tang.hongxian.end: In the histories Xue Song dies in 773 and Tian Chengsi seizes Xiangzhou two years later; the court's punitive campaign fails, and the three Hebei garrisons stay hereditary for over a century.
shots: In the Luzhou commander's residence the governor sits alone at night, sighing at the watch drums
A maid in black comes in: why is my master troubled
She binds her hair in a high knot, tucks a dragon-patterned dagger at her breast and vanishes into the night
In the Weibo bedchamber Tian Chengsi snores like thunder, a golden box at his bedside
The box in hand, she is back in Luzhou before the morning bell
tang.hongxian.title: Red Thread Steals the Golden Box: Weibo and Zhaoyi

tang.huangchao.end: Tang and the Shatuo retake Chang'an, Zhu Wen defects, and Huang Chao dies in 884; the Tang survives only in name.
shots: Crowds on the salt roads in a year of famine
Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao rise in revolt
A thousand-li campaign south to Lingnan and back north
Winter 880: they enter Chang'an
The whole city clad in golden armour
tang.huangchao.title: A Heaven-Piercing Fragrance: Huang Chao Takes Chang'an

tang.huichang.end: Xuanzong executes Zhao Guizhen and restores some temples, but Buddhism never regains its early Tang glory; Ennin returns to Japan in 847 and his diary becomes a priceless record of late Tang life.
shots: At the Zisheng temple in Chang'an a Japanese monk records the day's edict by lamplight
Temple halls are torn down and bronze Buddhas hauled away to be melted into coins
Tens of thousands of monks and nuns take off their robes and walk out of the temple gates
He too changes into lay clothes and leaves the city gate with sutras on his back
The next spring a bell tolls from the palace: the emperor who took elixirs is dead
tang.huichang.title: The Huichang Suppression: Ennin's Eyewitness

tang.hulao.end: The Xia army collapses; shown the captive Dou Jiande, Wang Shichong surrenders Luoyang.
shots: Tang siege lines around Luoyang
The Prince of Qin takes 3,500 men east to hold Hulao
The Xia army forms up over twenty li from morning to noon
The prince leads light cavalry straight into the Xia lines
At Niukouzhu Dou Jiande falls from his horse and is captured
tang.hulao.title: Hulao: Two Kings Captured in One Battle

tang.jianzhen.end: Jianzhen reaches Nara, sets up the ordination platform at Tōdai-ji, founds Tōshōdai-ji and dies there in 763, honoured in Japan as the Great Master who crossed the sea.
shots: At the Daming Temple in Yangzhou two Japanese monks kneel before an old master
First, second, third attempt — each time the ship is seized by officials or smashed by waves
On the fifth voyage a gale drives the ship to Hainan Island
On the way back Eiei dies and the old monk loses his sight
On the sixth voyage an envoy ship lands at Satsuma and the blind old man steps ashore
tang.jianzhen.title: Six Crossings to Japan: Jianzhen Sails East

tang.libai.end: Gao Lishi tells Lady Yang a line compares her to Zhao Feiyan, the emperor's offers of office are blocked, and Li Bai leaves Chang'an with a gift of gold, soon meeting the younger Du Fu in Luoyang.
shots: At the Ziji Temple in Chang'an an old man finishes reading "The Hard Road to Shu" and unhooks his golden tortoise to trade for wine
At the Chenxiang Pavilion the peonies bloom and the emperor sends men to the taverns to find Li Bai
Helped into the palace and splashed with cold water, he lifts his brush through bleary eyes
He stretches out a foot for Gao Lishi to pull off his boot
Clouds long for her robes, flowers for her face; the poem is done and the hall falls silent
tang.libai.title: The Banished Immortal: Li Bai in Chang'an

tang.luobinwang.end: Xu Jingye turns south instead of marching on Luoyang and is crushed within three months; Luo Binwang vanishes — killed, drowned, or fled to become a monk.
shots: In Yangzhou the banner to restore the Prince of Luling goes up and more than a hundred thousand enlist
In headquarters a middle-aged scholar drafts a proclamation
In the Luoyang palace the empress dowager reads the opening lines with a smile
At "the earth on the tomb is not yet dry, to whom is the orphan entrusted" her face changes
She sets it down: how could the chief ministers have missed such a man
tang.luobinwang.title: The Call to Arms against Wu Zhao: Luo Binwang

tang.shangguan.end: Shen never challenges Song again; a year later in the Tanglong coup Wan'er greets Li Longji with candles and her draft will but is beheaded beneath the banner, and Xuanzong later has her writings collected in twenty scrolls.
shots: On the last day of the first month a festooned tower rises before the tent-hall by Kunming Lake, over a hundred court poems piled below
A woman climbs the tower and reads them page by page
Rejected poems drift down from the tower and the poets each pick up their own
Only two men remain below, Shen Quanqi and Song Zhiwen, gazing up
The last page flutters down: it is Shen Quanqi's
tang.shangguan.title: Weighing the Talents of the Realm: Shangguan Wan'er

tang.suiyang.end: The starving city falls in the tenth month; Zhang Xun and thirty-six others die defiant, and relief arrives three days late, but the south is saved.
shots: Suiyang, gateway to the Yangtze–Huai region
At Yongqiu straw men lowered at night draw hundreds of thousands of arrows
Lei Wanchun stands on the wall with six arrows in his face
Nan Jiyun breaks out to beg for help at Linhuai
He shoots an arrow into a pagoda, half its shaft sunk in brick
tang.suiyang.title: Suiyang: Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan

tang.wangbo.end: Wang Bo adds a poem to his preface; the next year he falls into the sea crossing to Jiaozhi and dies of shock, remembered as one of the Four Paragons of early Tang.
shots: On the ninth day of the ninth month a feast fills the Tengwang Pavilion above the Gan River, autumn water stretching to the sky
The governor has paper and brush carried round for a preface; the guests all decline
A young man in his twenties takes the brush and begins at once
The governor withdraws to change and has each sentence reported to him
Sunset clouds fly with a lone wild duck; autumn water shares one colour with the endless sky
tang.wangbo.title: Sunset Clouds and a Lone Duck: The Preface to the Tengwang Pavilion

tang.weishui.end: Illig is captured and the Eastern Turks fall; the old emperor rejoices and the steppe peoples hail Taizong as Heavenly Khagan.
shots: Turkic camps on the north bank of the Wei
Emperor Taizong rides to the river with six horsemen
On the bridge a white horse is sacrificed to seal the pact
Four years later three thousand horsemen ride out of Mayi in the snow
Through fog in the Yin mountains they strike the khagan's tent
tang.weishui.title: The Wei River Pact: Li Jing Defeats the Turks

tang.weizheng.end: Taizong says he has lost a mirror, yet soon suspects Wei Zheng of faction and topples his stele, until returning from the failed Korean campaign he sighs that Wei Zheng would have stopped him and has it raised again.
shots: In the Taiji Hall a slight minister keeps speaking despite the emperor's darkening face
After court the emperor fumes: one day I will kill that country bumpkin
The empress stands in the courtyard in court robes and congratulates him: a wise lord makes upright ministers
When Wei Zheng lies dying the emperor brings the crown prince to his house, which lacks even a main hall
The emperor pulls down the stele he himself wrote, then orders it raised again
tang.weizheng.title: A Man as a Mirror: Wei Zheng

tang.wencheng.end: Songtsen Gampo bows as a son-in-law, adopts Tang dress and builds her a city; Tang–Tibetan contacts flourish.
shots: The bridal procession outside Chang'an
Gar Tongtsen offers gold to ask for a princess
The carriages cross the Riyue mountains heading west
By the Baihai lake the Tsenpo greets her in person
A city is built for the princess
tang.wencheng.title: Princess Wencheng Goes to Tibet

tang.wuzetian.end: Emperor Zhongzong is restored and Tang returns; Wu Zetian dies that year, renouncing the imperial title in her will.
shots: The Hall of Light in the divine capital Luoyang
In 690 the Tang becomes the Zhou
Di Renjie recommends Zhang Jianzhi
First month of 705: imperial guards enter the palace
At the Qianling tomb, a stele without words
tang.wuzetian.title: The Blank Stele: Wu Zetian

tang.xiantian.end: Princess Taiping dies at home, her sons and partisans executed except Xue Chongjian, her wealth rivalling the imperial treasury, and in the twelfth month the era becomes Kaiyuan.
shots: In the Chang'an palace the chief ministers all head to the princess's mansion after court
An informer reports: the princess plans for the guards to storm the palace from the Wude Hall on the fourth day of the seventh month
On the third the young emperor leads three hundred men from the Wude Hall through the Qianhua Gate
The retired emperor climbs the Chengtian Gate tower and hears the fighting below
Three days later the princess is brought back from a mountain temple and ordered to die
tang.xiantian.title: The Xiantian Coup: Princess Taiping

tang.xuanwu.end: Jiancheng and Yuanji are killed; Li Shimin becomes crown prince three days later and emperor in the eighth month.
shots: The northern Xuanwu Gate of the Chang'an palace
Night council in the Prince of Qin's mansion
At dawn Jiancheng and Yuanji enter the palace
At Linhu Hall they sense danger and turn their horses
The Xuanwu Gate
tang.xuanwu.title: The Xuanwu Gate Incident

tang.xuanzang.end: In 645 Xuanzang returns with 657 texts, writes the Record of the Western Regions and translates for nineteen years.
shots: Five beacon towers beyond Yumen Pass
Passing a beacon at night, an arrow flies at him
In the Moheyan desert his waterskin spills
The king of Gaochang comes out to greet him
At Nalanda, mountains of scriptures
tang.xuanzang.title: Journey West: Xuanzang's Pilgrimage

tang.yanzhenqing.end: Li Xilie's men hold him back; in the eighth month of 784 eunuchs strangle him at the Longxing temple in Caizhou at seventy-seven, and Emperor Dezong suspends court for five days.
shots: Changshan falls and its governor, taken to Luoyang, curses An Lushan to his face
Two years later in an office in Puzhou, Yan Zhenqing has only a wooden box holding his nephew's skull
He writes the elegy; at "the father captured, the son dead, the nest overturned, the eggs smashed" his brush grows wild, crossing out and writing again
Over twenty years later in Caizhou the rebel piles firewood in the courtyard to burn the old man in his seventies
The old man straightens his robe and cap and walks straight toward the fire
tang.yanzhenqing.title: Draft Elegy for My Nephew: Yan Zhenqing

wudai.chenqiao.end: The Zhou emperor abdicates and Zhao Kuangyin founds the Song; the capital stays orderly throughout.
shots: Kaifeng in the first month
Reports of a Northern Han and Khitan invasion
Night camp at Chenqiao Station
At dawn the officers stand in the courtyard with drawn swords
The yellow robe
wudai.chenqiao.title: The Yellow Robe: the Chenqiao Mutiny

wudai.dacaogu.end: Yelü Deguang dies at Luancheng and his body is salted for the journey north; Liu Zhiyuan enters Daliang and founds Later Han.
shots: Daliang in snow, gates open, Khitan cavalry filing in
In Chongyuan Hall the Khitan emperor holds court in Chinese robes
Horsemen plunder the villages and people flee to the hills
At Taiyuan a governor is proclaimed emperor by his men
On the road home the Khitan emperor collapses at Luancheng
wudai.dacaogu.title: Foraging Raids: Yelü Deguang Enters Bian

wudai.gaoping.end: Northern Han is routed; Shizong executes Fan Aineng and seventy officers and reforms the guards, and Zhao Kuangyin is promoted.
shots: Bagong plain at Gaoping in Zezhou
Feng Dao objects: can Your Majesty be a mountain?
The right wing breaks; Fan Aineng flees south with his cavalry
Shizong braves arrows and stones to lead the fight
Zhao Kuangyin charges with two thousand men
wudai.gaoping.title: The Battle of Gaoping: Emperor Shizong of Zhou

wudai.hanxizai.end: Han Xizai never becomes chief minister and dies in 970; the surviving Night Banquet scroll is a Song-dynasty copy in the Palace Museum.
shots: Two young men raise cups in farewell on the Huai River
Thirty years later Han's house in Jinling blazes with candles
A painter hides behind a screen, memorising everything
A dancer performs the Liuyao while the host beats the drum
After the party the host sits alone as a long scroll unrolls on the table
wudai.hanxizai.title: The Night Banquet: Han Xizai

wudai.huangqi.end: Guo Wei takes the throne as founder of Zhou in 951; his own sons dead, he leaves the throne to his adopted son Chai Rong.
shots: At Ye a secret edict reaches the army supervisor
News from the capital: Guo Wei's family has been killed
The army marches south across the Yellow River
Marching north against Liao, the army halts at Chanzhou
Soldiers tear down a yellow banner and wrap it around him
wudai.huangqi.title: The Yellow Banner at Chanzhou: Guo Wei

wudai.liyu.end: Li Yu spends his last three years in Bianjing and dies in 978; his lyrics written after the fall live on for a thousand years.
shots: Spring blossoms fill the palace gardens of Jinling
Fan Ruoshui boats at Caishi measuring the river
A pontoon bridge is finished; Song troops cross as if on land
Jinling falls; the last ruler surrenders bare-shouldered
The east wind returned to the small tower last night
wudai.liyu.title: Spring Flowers and Autumn Moon: Li Yu

wudai.qianliu.end: The sea wall protects Hangzhou's fields; Wuyue lasts three generations and peacefully submits to Song, sparing the region from war.
shots: The Qiantang bore in the eighth month, waves like snowy mountains
The new earthen wall is breached again and again
Workers fill bamboo cages with stones and sink them layer by layer
The king of Wuyue stands on the bank watching the tide
A letter home: the flowers are blooming on the paths, come back slowly
wudai.qianliu.title: The Sea Wall: Qian Liu

wudai.sanshi.end: Guo Congqian rebels; Zhuangzong is killed by an arrow and his body burned under musical instruments, eighteen years after his triumph.
shots: Three arrows before the coffin in the Jinyang palace
Thick fog at the siege camp; Jin troops break in
Into Bian, the end of Liang
Actors in greasepaint perform in the palace
A stray arrow outside the Xingjiao Gate
wudai.sanshi.title: Three Arrows: Li Cunxu

wudai.yanyun.end: The Sixteen Prefectures pass to the Khitan, leaving the northern frontier open for four centuries.
shots: Taiyuan, looking north to Yanmen
Night council in Hedong; Sang Weihan drafts the petition
Khitan cavalry ride south
At Jin'an the Tang army collapses
Sixteen prefectures cut from the map
wudai.yanyun.title: The Sixteen Prefectures: Shi Jingtang

wudai.zhuwen.end: Zhu Quanyu warns his brother that destroying the Tang will doom his clan; the deposed Tang emperor is murdered the next year.
shots: Overnight Baima Station on the Yellow River fills with soldiers
Over thirty court officials in purple and red are led to the riverbank
A failed examinee makes a cold remark beside them
In Jinxiang Hall at Daliang a Tang minister carries in the imperial seal
At a feast his elder brother smashes the dice into a bowl
wudai.zhuwen.title: Baima Station: Zhu Wen Usurps the Tang

xia.kongjia.end: Liu Lei flees in fear to Lu county; the Annals note Kongjia died, and three reigns later Jie lost the Xia.
shots: The palace pool churns; scales glint below the surface
Kongjia burns incense at the altar, consulting the spirits
A man who claims he can rear dragons walks through the palace gate
At the poolside a female dragon stops moving
He flees the Xia capital overnight
xia.kongjia.title: The Dragon-Keeper: Kongjia

xia.meixi.end: Shi Su warns Duke Xian of Jin with the tale of Meixi; the duke ignores him and Jin nearly falls to the Liji crisis.
shots: Xia chariots roll into the valleys of Youshi
The Youshi people present a young woman to end the war
Palace lanterns and endless music
Jie attacks Minshan and brings back two more women
By the Luo River a woman boards a small boat alone
xia.meixi.title: The Daughter of Youshi: Meixi

xia.mingtiao.end: Jie flees and dies in exile; Tang becomes Son of Heaven and Shang replaces Xia.
shots: The Xia capital Zhenxun, palaces before distant hills
At Bo, Yi Yin counsels Tang
Tang addresses his troops: the Xia has many crimes
The Xia army is broken; Jie flees to Mingtiao
On the field of Mingtiao a great banner sweeps down
xia.mingtiao.title: Mingtiao: Tang Overthrows the Xia

xia.qi.end: The Youhu are destroyed and all come to court; from now the throne passes from father to son.
shots: Below Mount Kuaiji, Yu's funeral carriage moves away
Yi withdraws south of Mount Ji, yielding to Yu's son
The chieftains' carriages turn to Qi's gate
The Youhu clan refuses; two armies face each other at Gan
Qi proclaims the Oath at Gan
xia.qi.title: The Family Realm: Qi Succeeds Yu

xia.shaokang.end: Ao and Yi fall one after the other; Shaokang restores Yu's legacy and the Xia sacrifices continue.
shots: The Xia capital in ruins, smoke rising beneath distant hills
Yi the archer trusts his bow; Han Zhuo seizes his household
Lady Min escapes through a hole in the wall and flees to Youreng
Shaokang serves as herdsman and cook, with one plot of land and one band of men
Nü Ai slips into Ao's camp: one arrow splits the night
xia.shaokang.title: The Restoration of Shaokang

xihan.baideng.end: Modu opens one corner; Gaozu escapes and pardons Liu Jing, and Han makes marriage peace with the Xiongnu.
shots: A bitter winter of rain and snow; two or three in ten soldiers lose fingers
The Xiongnu hide their best men and horses, showing only the weak
On Baideng hill Xiongnu horsemen surround them on every side
Han envoys send lavish gifts to the queen
In thick fog, crossbows loaded with two bolts march out through the open corner
xihan.baideng.title: The Siege of Baideng: Seven Days at Pingcheng

xihan.beishui.end: Zhao panics at the flags and is crushed; Chen Yu is killed and the king captured, and Han Xin treats Li Zuoche as his teacher.
shots: In the Taihang mountains, the narrow pass of Jingxing
Li Zuoche offers a plan; Chen Yu refuses it
At midnight two thousand light horsemen with red flags watch from the hills
Ten thousand men form up with their backs to the river; Zhao laughs
Suddenly the Zhao ramparts are covered in red Han flags
xihan.beishui.title: Back to the River: Jingxing

xihan.chentang.end: Zhizhi's head is sent to Chang'an; after long debate the emperor pardons the forged order and rewards both commanders.
shots: An earthen fort on the Talas River in Kangju
Chen Tang grips his sword and shouts down Gan Yanshou
Forty thousand men in six divisions
Fire outside the wooden wall; the chanyu's wives shoot from the ramparts
The chanyu is beheaded
xihan.chentang.title: Whoever Offends Mighty Han: Chen Tang

xihan.dongfangshuo.end: Emperor Wu bursts out laughing — asked to blame himself, he has praised himself — and gives him a dan of wine and a hundred jin of meat to take home to his wife.
shots: In the petition office two men carry in a huge bundle of writing tablets that fills half the room
On the midsummer feast day meat is to be handed out, but the steward is late and the gentlemen stand waiting
One man draws his sword, cuts off a piece of meat, tucks it in his robe and strolls away
Next day the emperor, stony-faced, orders him to confess his fault
He bows twice: taking the gift without waiting — how rude! cutting the meat with a sword — how bold!
xihan.dongfangshuo.title: Meat for His Wife: Dongfang Shuo

xihan.gaixia.end: Xiang Yu gives his horse to the ferryman, fights on foot, and cuts his own throat.
shots: Gaixia, ramparts layer upon layer
At night songs of Chu rise on every side
Drinking in the tent, singing in grief
Eight hundred horsemen break out and fight at Dongcheng
The Wu River
xihan.gaixia.title: Chu Songs on All Sides: Gaixia

xihan.gujian.end: Empress Xu dies; after Huo Guang's death the plot comes out, the Huo clan is wiped out, and her son eventually reigns as Emperor Yuan.
shots: In Chang'an's Shangguan ward a young couple live in a poor lane, an old sword hanging on the wall
In Weiyang Palace the ministers propose making the regent's youngest daughter empress
The emperor issues a strange edict: find the old sword I used in my humble days
After the empress gives birth, a woman physician brings her a bowl of pills
The empress asks: my head is spinning — is there poison in this medicine?
xihan.gujian.title: The Old Sword: Xu Pingjun

xihan.hanxin.end: Yong is defeated at Chencang and two kings surrender; the king of Han turns east and the Chu–Han war begins.
shots: Mountains of Nanzheng, the plank roads burned
Han Xin flees at night along a moonlit mountain road
Xiao He has no time to tell the king and pursues him himself
An altar is built and Han Xin is named chief general
The Han army takes the old road and strikes Chencang
xihan.hanxin.title: Chasing Han Xin by Moonlight: Secret Crossing to Chencang

xihan.hongmen.end: Zhang Liang offers jade in apology; Fan Zeng smashes the jade cup: the man who takes Xiang Yu's realm will be Liu Bang.
shots: Hongmen at Xinfeng and Bashang, two armies facing each other
Xiang Bo rides through the night to Liu Bang's camp
The feast: Xiang Yu and Xiang Bo face east, Fan Zeng faces south
Xiang Zhuang draws his sword and dances; Xiang Bo rises and dances too
Fan Kuai bursts into the tent
xihan.hongmen.title: The Feast at Hongmen: Xiang Zhuang's Sword Dance

xihan.huoguang.end: Liu He is sent home and his officials executed; Huo Guang enthrones Liu Bingyi as Emperor Xuan, and Liu He later dies as Marquis of Haihun in Yuzhang.
shots: In the Chengming hall of Weiyang Palace the officials sit in rows while one minister stands with his hand on his sword
The empress dowager sits in a pearl-sewn robe inside a military tent, guards with halberds on either side
The Master of Writing kneels and reads the memorial, item after item, for a long time
The young emperor lies prostrate on the floor as his seals and ribbons are removed
The palace gate shuts and more than two hundred of his old Changyi officials are led to the execution ground
xihan.huoguang.title: Twenty-Seven Days: Huo Guang Deposes the Prince of Changyi

xihan.jiayi.end: The emperor admits he had thought himself Jia Yi's superior and was wrong; Jia Yi becomes tutor to the Prince of Liang, and when the prince dies in a riding fall he grieves himself to death at thirty-three.
shots: In the Chang'an court a scholar barely twenty answers every question while the old ministers exchange glances
On the Xiang river, in a small boat, the exile casts a rhapsody into the water
In his bedroom at Changsha an owl flies in and settles by his seat
In the Xuanshi hall of Weiyang Palace, late at night with the candles low, the emperor shifts his mat forward
What the emperor asks about is not the common people but ghosts and spirits
xihan.jiayi.title: Night Audience in the Xuanshi Hall: Jia Yi

xihan.liguang.end: Refusing to face the clerks' interrogation at past sixty, Li Guang cuts his own throat; the whole army weeps, and Sima Qian writes that the peach and plum say nothing yet a path forms beneath them.
shots: In the dusk of Youbeiping a dark shape lies in the grass; the general draws his bow to full
Next morning the shaft is buried deep in a rock, its head no longer visible
An old general asks a diviner: why have I never been made a marquis?
North of the desert the cavalry of the eastern route circle in the wasteland, their guide long gone
In his tent he tells his officers: since I bound up my hair I have fought the Xiongnu more than seventy times
xihan.liguang.title: Li Guang, Never Ennobled: An Arrow in the Stone

xihan.mobei.end: Huo Qubing sacrifices at Mount Langjuxu and reaches the northern sea; the Xiongnu flee and no royal court remains south of the desert.
shots: The desert, an endless horizon
Two armies leave the frontier from Dingxiang and Dai
Wugang wagons ring into a fortified camp
A great wind rises, gravel lashes faces
Mount Langjuxu
xihan.mobei.title: Sacrifice at Mount Langjuxu: the Battle of Mobei

xihan.qiguo.end: The starving Wu army retreats and is routed; the king of Wu is killed by the Eastern Yue, and all seven states fall within three months.
shots: Beacon fires flare across the eastern states
Eastern Market: Chao Cuo is executed in court robes
Zhou Yafu rides relay carriages and detours through Wu Pass
Deep walls at Changyi; Wu troops rush the south-east corner
Light cavalry cut the Huai–Si junction and Wu runs out of grain
xihan.qiguo.title: The Rebellion of the Seven States: Zhou Yafu

xihan.simaqian.end: Sima Qian completes his 130 chapters, 526,500 characters, the book later known as the Shiji, explaining he endured disgrace so his writing would not be lost to later ages.
shots: In Luoyang the dying Grand Historian grips his son's hand, tears streaming down his face
In the front hall of Weiyang Palace all the officials echo the emperor; only one man speaks up for Li Ling
In the dark "silkworm chamber" he huddles in a corner
Bamboo scrolls pile up roll after roll, from the Yellow Emperor down to the present reign
A long letter ends: store it in the famous mountains and pass it to the right people
xihan.simaqian.title: Writing in Wrath: Sima Qian

xihan.simaxiangru.end: The emperor learns the author is alive and summons Sima Xiangru, who writes the Shanglin rhapsody, becomes a court gentleman and later opens the southwest to Han.
shots: At the Zhuo family feast in Linqiong hundreds of guests sit, the county magistrate himself among them
An elegant guest plays the qin while someone listens from behind a screen
Late at night a woman pushes open the back gate and runs out into the moonlight
In a small Linqiong wine shop the mistress tends the counter while the master, in an apron, washes the cups
In the Chang'an palace the emperor reads a rhapsody and asks why he cannot live in the same age as its author
xihan.simaxiangru.title: Selling Wine at the Counter: Sima Xiangru and Zhuo Wenjun

xihan.suwu.end: When Han asks for him the Xiongnu claim he is dead; told of a letter tied to a goose, the chanyu relents and Su Wu returns home.
shots: An empty frozen plain by the Northern Sea
Wei Lü raises a sword; Su Wu stabs himself with his own knife
In a cellar he eats snow with felt
He herds sheep holding the Han tally until its tassels fall away
Li Ling pours wine and weeps
xihan.suwu.title: Herding Sheep by the Northern Sea: Su Wu

xihan.tiying.end: Emperor Wen abolishes tattooing, nose-cutting and foot-cutting, replacing them with flogging and labour; Chunyu Yi is pardoned and returns to Qi to practise medicine.
shots: Outside Linzi the prison cart sets off, and a man turns to curse his five weeping daughters
The youngest dries her tears and follows the cart onto the westward road
Beneath the palace gates of Chang'an a girl kneels and offers up a bundle of bamboo slips
In the hall the emperor reads the slips and stays silent for a long time
The edict goes out: mutilating punishments are abolished
xihan.tiying.title: Tiying's Petition: Ending Mutilating Punishments

xihan.wugu.end: The prince hangs himself and Empress Wei dies; later Emperor Wu realises the injustice, wipes out Jiang Chong's clan and builds a terrace of longing.
shots: A hot summer outside Ganquan Palace
Jiang Chong digs up a wooden doll
Shi De warns the prince of the fate of Fusu
Five days of fighting in Chang'an; tens of thousands die
At Quanjiu in Hu county, the door is shut
xihan.wugu.title: The Witchcraft Affair: Crown Prince Li

xihan.zhangqian.end: Over a hundred set out and only two come back; Zhang Qian's reports open Han contact with the Western Regions.
shots: The long road west outside Chang'an
Out from Longxi, through Xiongnu land, captured
Over ten years he never lets go of the Han tally
West to Dayuan, Kangju and the Yuezhi
The return
xihan.zhangqian.title: Opening the West: Zhang Qian's Mission

xihan.zhaojun.end: Titled Ninghu Yanzhi, she bears a son; after Huhanye dies she remarries by steppe custom, and the frontier is quiet for decades.
shots: Deep within the palace of Chang'an
Huhanye Chanyu comes to court
At the farewell Zhaojun, radiant, lights up the Han palace
The carriages head north beyond the frontier
She looks back toward Chang'an as the frontier wind rises
xihan.zhaojun.title: Zhaojun Beyond the Frontier

xizhou.feizi.end: King Xiao enfeoffs Feizi at Qin as a vassal to continue the Ying sacrifices; peace holds with the western Rong.
shots: Horses gallop in the wind on the Quanqiu grasslands
A young man checks the mares one by one
Pastures stretch out of sight between the Qian and Wei rivers
An envoy of the Zhou king arrives at the stud
The king grants him a piece of land called Qin
xizhou.feizi.title: Between the Qian and Wei: Feizi the Horse Breeder

xizhou.gantang.end: The people remember the Duke's rule, refuse to cut the tree, and compose the ode 'Gantang'.
shots: A pear tree in white blossom on the plain of Shan
The Duke of Shao sits beneath it hearing a land dispute
He travels through every village and never stays in official lodgings
Years later someone walks toward the tree with an axe
The axe stops mid-air as villagers begin to sing
xizhou.gantang.title: The Pear Tree: the Duke of Shao

xizhou.gonghe.end: The dukes of Shao and Zhou rule jointly, called Gonghe; fourteen years later Li dies and King Xuan succeeds.
shots: Hao: people walk the streets in silence
King Li loves profit and trusts Duke Rong Yi
A shaman of Wei watches for critics; people only exchange glances on the road
In the third year the people surround the palace
The king flees to Zhi; two dukes govern
xizhou.gonghe.title: First Year of Gonghe: the People's Revolt

xizhou.haojing.end: King You dies below Mount Li and Hao is ruined; King Ping moves east to Luoyi and Western Zhou ends.
shots: A beacon tower on Mount Li
Bao Si does not smile
The beacon is lit, the lords arrive, but there is no enemy
The Marquis of Shen and the Quanrong attack; the beacon is lit again and no one comes
At the foot of Mount Li
xizhou.haojing.title: Beacon Fires: the Fall of Hao

xizhou.hezun.end: Chengzhou is completed; the He zun inscription contains the first known use of 'zhongguo', the centre of the world.
shots: Morning mist between the Luo and Yi rivers
The Duke of Shao divines the city site with turtle shells by the river
The Duke of Zhou holds a plan and measures the line of the walls
The new city is finished; King Cheng instructs the young clansmen in the hall
Inside a bronze vessel four characters are cast: 'dwelling in the centre'
xizhou.hezun.title: Dwelling in the Centre: Building Chengzhou

xizhou.muwang.end: Zaofu races the king home to put down the revolt and is enfeoffed with Zhao; the western tribes stop paying tribute.
shots: At Hao's western gate eight horses stand in the mist
Zhai Gong Moufu warns: former kings showed virtue, not arms
Campaign against the Quanrong: four white wolves and four white deer
Zaofu holds the reins as they ride west to Kunlun
Urgent news from the east: King Yan of Xu has rebelled
xizhou.muwang.title: Eight Steeds: King Mu Rides West

xizhou.xuanwang.end: The lords return to Zhou in the Xuan revival, yet cracks widen until the royal army is defeated at Qianmu.
shots: Xianyun horsemen raise dust on the northern plateau
At Hao the young King Xuan dons armour and mounts his chariot
In the sixth month the chariots ride out to Taiyuan
Yin Jifu returns with heads and captives
The campaign is cast on a bronze basin
xizhou.xuanwang.title: Striking the Xianyun: King Xuan's Revival

xizhou.zhaowang.end: Three centuries later Guan Zhong asks Chu about King Zhao, and Chu replies: ask the riverbank.
shots: The broad Han River, Chu forests on the southern bank
The Zhou fleet crosses in great numbers
The sky darkens suddenly; birds and beasts flee
In midstream a boat starts coming apart
Six armies sink into the Han; only banners float on the water
xizhou.zhaowang.title: The King Who Never Returned: King Zhao

xizhou.zhougong.end: After seven years the Duke returns power; King Cheng reads the prayer, weeps and welcomes him in person.
shots: Candlelight flickers in the palace at Feng and Hao
King Wu falls ill; the Duke of Zhou sets up an altar and writes a prayer
King Cheng is a child; rumours spread through the realm
Three years of campaigning east of Yin
Thunder, lightning and wind flatten the crops; the metal casket is opened
xizhou.zhougong.title: The Metal Casket: the Duke of Zhou's Eastern Campaign

yuan.chengjisi.end: Genghis Khan organises the tribes into units of a thousand and the Mongols rise.
shots: The steppe and the Onon River
Börte is abducted; sworn brothers join forces
Sworn brothers turn enemies
The Keraites fall, the Naimans fall
The nine-tailed white standard
yuan.chengjisi.title: Genghis Khan: the Source of the Onon

yuan.dadu.end: Dadu's walls run sixty li with eleven gates; the Tonghui canal brings southern barges to Jishuitan, and Ming–Qing Beijing is built on Dadu.
shots: A lake and wasteland beside the ruins of Jin Zhongdu
An old former monk draws a square city on the ground
Eleven gates, one central axis, the palace built around the lake
Water from Baifu spring loops along the foot of the hills into the city
Grain barges sail into Jishuitan, masts like a forest
yuan.dadu.title: Dadu: Liu Bingzhong

yuan.guanhanqing.end: In the play all three vows come true and Dou E is cleared when her father becomes an inspector; the drama becomes the classic Chinese tragedy, while Guan Hanqing's life survives in only a few lines.
shots: In the theatres of Dadu, clappers and drums strike up and the stands are packed
Backstage a middle-aged writer revises lyrics while rehearsing with an actress
On stage a young woman is led to the execution ground, a death placard on her back
She lifts her face and cries out three vows, and the sky goes dark
Snow falls from a June sky and blood spatters a twelve-foot length of white silk
yuan.guanhanqing.title: The Injustice to Dou E: Guan Hanqing

yuan.hongjin.end: The Red Turbans sweep the north; Zhu Yuanzhang, risen from their ranks, founds the Ming and Xu Da takes Dadu as the Yuan emperor flees north.
shots: The Yellow River bursts its banks, flooding a thousand li
Jia Lu repairs the river with over a hundred thousand labourers
A one-eyed stone man is dug from the riverbed
At Yingzhou, red headscarves
The realm rises
yuan.hongjin.title: One-Eyed Stone Man: the Red Turbans

yuan.huangdaopo.end: Wunijing quilts become famous; when Huang Daopo dies the villagers bury her and build her a shrine, and Songjiang becomes China's cotton centre.
shots: Kapok blossoms turn the hills of Yazhou on Hainan red
Li women spin under a bamboo house while a Han woman learns beside them
A ship sails north with the now-elderly woman at the bow
Wunijing village women pick seeds by hand and bow the cotton, slow and tiring
A new three-spindle treadle wheel turns and patterns appear in the cloth
yuan.huangdaopo.title: Wunijing: Huang Daopo

yuan.makebolo.end: A Yongle Dadian record names the same three envoys Polo says escorted the princess west, showing his account has a reliable basis.
shots: Shangdu, a palace city on the steppe
Relay stations in sight of one another; envoys with tablets gallop past
Khanbaliq, streets laid out like a chessboard
Quanzhou harbour: fourteen four-masted ships
Three names on a relay-station document
yuan.makebolo.title: Travels in the East: Marco Polo

yuan.shenfeng.end: Fan Wenhu abandons over a hundred thousand men on the islands; the Yuanshi says only three returned, and Kublai's plans for another attack are dropped.
shots: Warships gather at Happo in Goryeo
In 1274 Yuan troops land at Hakata Bay
In 1281 a hundred thousand troops from Jiangnan cross the sea
A great typhoon; warships smash into each other
Fan Wenhu picks the sturdiest ships and flees first
yuan.shenfeng.title: Across the Sea: the Yuan Invasions of Japan

yuan.shoushi.end: Finished in 1280 and issued in 1281, the Shoushi calendar sets the year at 365.2425 days, the same value used by the modern Gregorian calendar.
shots: In the Dadu observatory the old instruments are rusted
Guo Shoujing redesigns the simplified armillary
Surveys across the empire reach the South Sea
Under the tall gnomon the noon shadow falls on the scale
The new calendar is completed and named Shoushi
yuan.shoushi.title: The Shoushi Calendar: Guo Shoujing

yuan.xizheng.end: Genghis praises Jalal al-Din's daring; Khwarazm falls, Qiu Chuji urges reverence for Heaven and love of the people, and the army returns east.
shots: Camel bells of a caravan at Otrar
The Mongol army crosses the Altai
Jebe and Subutai chase Muhammad
On the Indus Jalal al-Din leaps into the river on horseback
At the Hindu Kush camp Qiu Chuji offers counsel
yuan.xizheng.title: The Western Campaign: Genghis Khan and Changchun

yuan.yelvchucai.end: Ögedei laughs at the treasure and asks if the south has another like him, and appoints Yelü Chucai head of the Secretariat that day.
shots: In the great tent ministers debate what to do with the newly won Han lands
A courtier says the Han are useless; drive them out and turn the fields into pasture
A long-bearded Khitan stands and unrolls a ledger
A bowyer holds up a bow and asks what use a Confucian is
A year later ten tax commissioners lay out silk, gold and granary records in the hall
yuan.yelvchucai.title: The Craftsman of Governance: Yelü Chucai

yuan.zhiyuan.end: The dynasty is named Great Yuan; the capital moves to Dadu and the Song falls in 1279, uniting the realm.
shots: Kaiping, where steppe meets farmland
News of Möngke's death arrives
Two khans at once: Kaiping and Karakorum
Four years of struggle
Great is the primal origin
yuan.zhiyuan.title: Zhiyuan: Kublai Founds the Yuan

zhanguo.changping.end: Zhao Kuo is shot dead in the fighting and Zhao is crushed; the burial of the surrendered troops is recorded, its scale disputed.
shots: The Shangdang highlands by the Dan River
Lian Po holds his walls through three years of stalemate
