Rumours in Handan: Qin fears only Zhao Kuo
Zhao Kuo attacks; Qin feigns retreat
Supply lines cut for forty-six days
zhanguo.changping.title: Strategy on Paper: the Battle of Changping

zhanguo.fanju.end: Fan Ju spares Xu Jia for the gift of a coarse silk robe but sends word to the King of Wei: send me Wei Qi's head; Wei Qi flees and finally takes his own life.
shots: In the Wei chancellor's mansion a retainer is beaten until his ribs break, rolled in a mat and dumped in the latrine
At night he crawls out of the mat; a friend hides him and he takes the name Zhang Lu
In a detached palace at Xianyang the King of Qin dismisses his attendants and kneels to ask
On the map his finger runs from Han and Wei to Qi and Chu: befriend the far, attack the near
Years later the Wei envoy Xu Jia kneels at the steps of the Qin chancellor's mansion and finally sees who the chancellor is
zhanguo.fanju.title: Befriend the Far, Attack the Near: Fan Ju Comes to Qin

zhanguo.ganluo.end: Zhao cedes five cities, Qin recalls Zhang Tang and the King of Qin makes Gan Luo a senior minister; after this the histories never mention him again.
shots: In the chancellor's mansion, Lü Buwei sits at his desk in silent displeasure
A boy steps forward: let me go and persuade Zhang Tang
At Zhang Tang's house the boy asks: how do your merits compare with Bai Qi's?
Outside the city, the King of Zhao comes out in person to greet the twelve-year-old Qin envoy
On the map five cities are circled in vermilion and pass to Qin
zhanguo.ganluo.title: A Senior Minister at Twelve: Gan Luo

zhanguo.hanfei.end: The pardon comes too late; Sima Qian grieves that the author of "The Difficulties of Persuasion" could not escape them himself, yet Han Fei's ideas guide Qin's unification.
shots: In the Xianyang palace the King of Qin puts down the slips: if I could meet this man I would die without regret
Li Si answers: it was written by Han Fei, a prince of Han
The Han envoy's carriage enters Xianyang; the man aboard stammers when he speaks
In the Yunyang prison a jailer brings a bowl of poison
When the pardon arrives the cell holds only a scroll of "The Difficulties of Persuasion"
zhanguo.hanfei.title: The Difficulties of Persuasion: The Death of Han Fei

zhanguo.hufu.end: Prince Zhang's revolt fails; besieged for three months, the abdicated king eats sparrow chicks and starves at Shaqiu.
shots: Nomad horsemen ride across the northern steppe
At court King Wuling appears in nomad dress
Prince Cheng pleads illness; the king visits his house in person
Mounted archers ride out from Dai to attack Zhongshan
The gates of Shaqiu Palace stay shut
zhanguo.hufu.title: Nomad Dress and Mounted Archery: King Wuling of Zhao

zhanguo.huoniu.end: The Yan army panics and Qi Jie is killed; all seventy cities return to Qi and Tian Dan welcomes King Xiang to Linzi.
shots: Over seventy Qi cities fall until only Ju and Jimo remain
On the walls of Jimo Tian Dan shares the work with his soldiers
Spies sow doubt in Yan; Yue Yi flees and Qi Jie replaces him
A thousand oxen with blades tied to horns and oiled reeds to tails
Holes cut in the wall; at night the burning oxen charge
zhanguo.huoniu.title: The Fire Oxen: Tian Dan Restores Qi

zhanguo.jiming.end: All the roosters crow and the gate opens; Qin pursuers arrive too late, and the retainers learn to respect the two humble guests.
shots: In the Xianyang palace the king of Qin sits opposite a prince of Qi
At night a retainer climbs the palace wall into the treasury
A white fox-fur robe is presented to the favourite concubine
Under false names the carriages race overnight to Hangu Pass
Below the pass a retainer throws back his head and crows like a rooster
zhanguo.jiming.title: Cock Crow and Dog Thief: Lord Mengchang Escapes

zhanguo.jingke.end: Jing Ke leans on a pillar laughing, the attempt failed; next year Qin takes Ji.
shots: The paper fades in, hills drawn stroke by stroke, vertical title
Yan palace: Crown Prince Dan and Jing Ke, Fan Wuqi's head in a box and the map of Dukang
Farewell at the Yi River: white robes, wind, water, the struck zhu
Xianyang palace: bronze pillars, the king, Qin Wuyang turning pale, the map presented
The map unrolls to reveal the dagger: one dry-brush slash, freeze-frame, two seals appear
zhanguo.jingke.title: Cold Waters of the Yi: Jing Ke Attempts to Kill the King of Qin

zhanguo.libing.end: With Dujiangyan, the Chengdu plain becomes a "Land of Abundance" free from flood and drought; an Eastern Han stone statue of Li Bing was excavated there in 1974.
shots: Where the Min leaves the mountains, the river rushes down thick with silt and half the farmland below lies flooded
The new governor stands on Mount Yulei, watching the current beneath him
Labourers fill bamboo cages with stones and sink them one by one mid-stream into a fish-mouth levee
On the cliff they burn firewood against the rock, douse it with cold water and the stone cracks apart
The Bottle-Neck is cut through, the river splits in two and clear water flows into the Chengdu plain
zhanguo.libing.title: Dujiangyan: Li Bing Tames the River

zhanguo.lvbuwei.end: Zichu reaches the Qin camp, later becomes King Zhuangxiang and makes Lü Buwei chancellor; when Ying Zheng succeeds, Lü is honoured as "Second Father".
shots: In the streets of Handan a shabby Qin hostage walks by with his head down, his carriage worn
A wealthy merchant watches him and murmurs: this is a rare commodity worth hoarding
At home the merchant asks his father: how many times profit from farming? from jade? from setting up a ruler?
In Xianyang, Lady Huayang accepts a cart of treasure and listens to tales of the hostage who longs for her
With Qin besieging Handan, the hostage slips out of the gate carrying six hundred jin of gold
zhanguo.lvbuwei.title: Rare Goods Worth Hoarding: Lü Buwei

zhanguo.maling.end: Pang Juan, outwitted and beaten, cuts his own throat; Qi crushes Wei and captures Crown Prince Shen, and Sun Bin becomes famous.
shots: A thousand li of plain between Daliang of Wei and Handan of Zhao
Sun Bin plans for Tian Ji from inside a covered cart
Guiling: the Wei army hurries home and is struck halfway
Qi enters Wei; a hundred thousand cooking fires shrink to fifty, then thirty thousand
Maling road: a torch is raised and ten thousand crossbows fire at once
zhanguo.maling.title: Besiege Wei to Save Zhao: Guiling and Maling

zhanguo.mengzi.end: King Hui cannot use his advice; he soon dies, and after meeting his successor Mencius remarks that he "does not look like a ruler" and leaves Wei.
shots: In the palace at Daliang, a white-haired ruler waits for a guest from afar
The king's first question: venerable sir, what profit will you bring my state?
Mencius follows the logic down: the king speaks of profit, then the ministers, then the gentlemen and commoners
The king falls silent; beyond the hall lies a Wei that has lost its crown prince on the battlefield
Mencius says: let Your Majesty speak only of humaneness and rightness — why speak of profit?
zhanguo.mengzi.title: Why Speak of Profit? Mencius Meets King Hui of Liang

zhanguo.qiefu.end: The Qin army lifts the siege; Hou Ying faces north and kills himself on the day the prince reaches Jin Bi's camp.
shots: Handan under siege, beacon smoke on the walls
Lord Pingyuan's letters keep coming, blaming Wei for not helping
At the Yi Gate, Hou Ying offers a plan
Lady Ru steals the military tally from the king's chamber
At Ye an iron mace strikes
zhanguo.qiefu.title: Stealing the Tally to Save Zhao: Lord Xinling

zhanguo.quyuan.end: Qu Yuan writes "Embracing the Sand", clasps a stone and drowns himself in the Miluo; Chu declines and falls to Qin within decades.
shots: The gate of Ying closes behind a man in a tall hat with a long sword, driven out of the city
Hair unbound, he walks the marsh shore chanting, his face haggard
A fisherman pauses his boat: aren't you the Lord of the Three Clans? how did you come to this?
News arrives that Ying has fallen; the northern sky burns red
At the Miluo river he picks up a stone and walks into the water
zhanguo.quyuan.title: Embracing the Sand: Qu Yuan

zhanguo.sanjia.end: Zhi Bo's army collapses and his clan is destroyed; fifty years later the Zhou king names Wei, Zhao and Han as states.
shots: The lone city of Jinyang by the Fen River
Zhi Bo demands land; Han and Wei yield, Zhao refuses
The city is flooded to within three planks of the top
At midnight Zhang Mengtan is lowered over the wall
The dikes are broken to flood Zhi Bo's camp instead
zhanguo.sanjia.title: Jinyang: the Partition of Jin

zhanguo.shangyang.end: Qin grows rich and strong; after Duke Xiao dies, Shang Yang is accused of treason, turned away at an inn, and torn apart.
shots: Outside Yueyang, the Guanzhong plain
Jing Jian brings Wei Yang to Duke Xiao
Court debate: Gan Long and Du Zhi against Wei Yang
At the south gate of the market a thirty-foot log is set up
A man moves the log and receives fifty pieces of gold
zhanguo.shangyang.title: Moving the Log: Shang Yang's Reforms

zhanguo.sujin.end: "Because you are now high and rich," she says; Su Qin hands out a thousand pieces of gold to his clan. The Shiji's claim that Qin dared not leave the Hangu Pass for fifteen years is widely thought exaggerated.
shots: At home in Luoyang, a man in a worn-out black sable coat comes to the door; his wife stays at her loom, his sister-in-law will not cook for him
Late at night he dozes over the slips and drives an awl into his own thigh
In the Yan palace he traces a line on the map linking six states
Zhao, Han, Wei, Qi, Chu: his carriage passes from court to court
Passing Luoyang again, his carts fill the road and his sister-in-law kneels by the roadside, afraid to look up
zhanguo.sujin.title: The Vertical Alliance: Su Qin Holds Six Seals

zhanguo.wanbi.end: Lin Xiangru is promoted above Lian Po; Lian Po later begs forgiveness carrying thorns, and general and minister are reconciled.
shots: Palaces of Handan before distant hills
A letter from Qin offers fifteen cities for the jade disc
At Zhangtai, Lin Xiangru holds the disc and backs against a pillar
At Mianchi the king of Qin asks the king of Zhao to play the zither
Within five paces
zhanguo.wanbi.title: Returning the Jade Intact: the Meeting at Mianchi

zhanguo.wuqi.end: Wu Qi dies under the arrows; King Su has more than seventy clans executed for wounding the royal corpse, and Chu's reforms die with him.
shots: Outside Ying, Wu Qi rides past newly opened fields, trailed by the carts of nobles moved off their fiefs
White banners hang in the Chu palace: King Dao is dead
At the palace gate, the royal kinsmen burst into the mourning hall with bows and crossbows
Driven to the bier, Wu Qi throws himself over the king's body
Arrows pour in, bristling from Wu Qi and striking the king's corpse too
zhanguo.wuqi.title: Shielded by a Corpse: The Death of Wu Qi

zhanguo.ximenbao.end: The officials kowtow until their foreheads bleed and no one in Ye mentions the River God's bride again; Ximen Bao sets the people to digging twelve canals that water their fields.
shots: On the bank of the Zhang, a red silk tent is pitched on the shoal and a girl is pushed inside
An old shaman leans on her staff, a dozen female disciples behind her, the elders and petty officials standing by
The new magistrate looks the girl over and shakes his head: she won't do, please go and tell the River God yourself
Constables lift the old shaman and throw her into the river
The magistrate waits on the bank, bowing, for a long time, then says: perhaps the elders should go and hurry her
zhanguo.ximenbao.title: The River God's Bride: Ximen Bao Governs Ye

zhanguo.zhangyi.end: In 312 BCE Chu is crushed at Danyang, eighty thousand beheaded and Qu Gai captured; a second all-out attack is defeated again at Lantian.
shots: In the hall at Ying, the Qin envoy unrolls a map and points to the Shang–Yu region
The ministers offer congratulations; one official alone looks grave
A Chu champion rides to the Qi border and insults the King of Qi to his face
In Xianyang, Zhang Yi emerges on a crutch: I have a fief of six li to offer Your Majesty
At Danyang the Chu banners fall and their commander is captured
zhanguo.zhangyi.title: Six Li of Land: Zhang Yi Cheats Chu

zhanguo.zhuangzi.end: Zhuangzi never takes office; his debate with Hui Shi on the bridge over the Hao about the happiness of fish becomes the most famous dialogue in Chinese philosophy.
shots: By the Pu river a thin man sits on a rock fishing, his rod perfectly still
Two Chu officials stand behind him holding gifts: the king wishes to entrust you with his state
Without turning he asks: I hear Chu has a sacred tortoise, dead three thousand years, kept in the ancestral hall
In the riverside mud a tortoise drags its tail slowly past
He waves them off: go, I would rather drag my tail in the mud
zhanguo.zhuangzi.title: Dragging Its Tail in the Mud: Zhuang Zhou
